class SimulationReplicates(list[SimulationResults]):
    """
    Replicates of a run of a stochastic engine, one `SimulationResults` each.

    A ``list`` of runs at the same positions, each with its own seed:
    ``replicates[i].seed`` repeats replicate ``i``. The statistics reduce the
    replicates position by position, and `member_statistics` reduces them as
    ``ci_percentiles`` requires.

    Attributes
    ----------
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    positions : list[float]
        Positions on the axis, shared by every replicate.
    """

    seed: int
    positions: list[float]

    def __init__(
        self, runs: Iterable[SimulationResults], seed: int, positions: Sequence[float]
    ):
        """
        Replicates of one run.

        Parameters
        ----------
        runs : Iterable[SimulationResults]
            One run per replicate, at `positions`.
        seed : int
            The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions on the axis, ascending.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a run is not at `positions`.
        """
        super().__init__(runs)
        self.seed = seed
        self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
        for index, run in enumerate(self):
            if run.positions != self.positions:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Replicate {index} is at other positions than the replicates."
                )

    @property
    def seeds(self) -> list[int]:
        """The seed of each replicate, in order."""
        return [run.seed for run in self if run.seed is not None]

    def _values(self, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        if not self:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        return np.asarray([run[name] for run in self], dtype=float)

    def mean(self) -> SimulationResults:
        """
        The mean of the replicates at each position, for each output.

        Returns
        -------
        SimulationResults
            One series of means per output, with no seed.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If there are no replicates.
        """
        names = list(self[0]) if self else []
        if not names:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        return SimulationResults(
            self.positions,
            {name: self._values(name).mean(axis=0).tolist() for name in names},
        )

    def quantiles(self, levels: Sequence[float]) -> dict[float, SimulationResults]:
        """
        Quantiles of the replicates at each position, for each output.

        The quantile is the one convention of commol (`weighted_quantiles`
        with equal weights, NumPy's ``method="hazen"``).

        Parameters
        ----------
        levels : Sequence[float]
            Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1, such as ``[0.05, 0.5,
            0.95]``.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[float, SimulationResults]
            The results of each level.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If a level is outside ``[0, 1]`` or there are no replicates.
        """
        for level in levels:
            if not 0.0 <= level <= 1.0:
                raise ValueError(f"A quantile level is between 0 and 1, got {level}.")
        if not self:
            raise ValueError("There are no replicates.")
        from commol.api.inference.intervals import weighted_quantiles

        names = list(self[0])
        per_name = {
            name: [
                weighted_quantiles(column.tolist(), levels)
                for column in self._values(name).T
            ]
            for name in names
        }
        return {
            level: SimulationResults(
                self.positions,
                {
                    name: [at_position[index] for at_position in per_name[name]]
                    for name in names
                },
            )
            for index, level in enumerate(levels)
        }

    def member_statistics(
        self, output: str, confidence_level: float
    ) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        """
        The spread of one output across the replicates, at each position.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output : str
            An output name.
        confidence_level : float
            Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[float]]
            Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
            ``max``, one value per position (`member_statistics`).

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If no replicate has the output.
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is out of range or there are no
            replicates.
        """
        from commol.api.inference.intervals import member_statistics

        if self and output not in self[0]:
            raise KeyError(
                f"'{output}' is not an output of the replicates. "
                f"Outputs: {sorted(self[0])}"
            )
        return member_statistics([run[output] for run in self], confidence_level)

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        """The number of replicates, their seed and their positions."""
        return (
            f"SimulationReplicates({len(self)} replicates, seed={self.seed!r}, "
            f"positions={self.positions!r})"
        )

def __init__(
    self, runs: Iterable[SimulationResults], seed: int, positions: Sequence[float]
):
    """
    Replicates of one run.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runs : Iterable[SimulationResults]
        One run per replicate, at `positions`.
    seed : int
        The seed the replicate seeds derive from.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions on the axis, ascending.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a run is not at `positions`.
    """
    super().__init__(runs)
    self.seed = seed
    self.positions = [float(position) for position in positions]
    for index, run in enumerate(self):
        if run.positions != self.positions:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Replicate {index} is at other positions than the replicates."
            )

def window_index(at: float, window: float) -> int:
    """
    Window a position belongs to.

    The exact inverse of :func:`window_end`, and the containing window for
    any position in between: ``max(ceil(at / window) - 1, 0)``. Position 0
    belongs to window 0. :func:`commol.api.reporting.observed_report` places
    each observation with this rule.

    Parameters
    ----------
    at : float
        A position on the axis.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Zero-based window index.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive or `at` is negative.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    if not at >= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"at must not be negative, got {at}.")
    return max(math.ceil(_windows_in(at, window)) - 1, 0)

def window_ends(window: float, end: float) -> list[float]:
    """
    Positions closing each complete window up to a position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    end : float
        Last position covered, such as the last position of a run.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        ``window``, ``2 * window``, ... up to `end`. A trailing partial window
        is not included.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    count = math.floor(_windows_in(end, window)) if end > 0 else 0
    return [window_end(index, window) for index in range(count)]

def windowed_totals(
    series: Sequence[float],
    positions: Sequence[float],
    window: float,
    at: Iterable[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Amount a cumulative series gained over each window.

    Each value is the series at the end of the window minus the series at its
    start, ``at - window``: the same quantity a calibration compares an
    observation against when that observation sets ``window``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    series : Sequence[float]
        A cumulative series, one value per position.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions of the series, ascending, such as
        ``SimulationResults.positions``.
    window : float
        Length of one window on the axis.
    at : Iterable[float] | None, optional
        Positions at which windows close. Defaults to every complete window of
        the series (:func:`window_ends`). Pass the observation positions to
        reproduce exactly the values a calibration used.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One increment per requested position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `window` is not positive, a window starts before position 0, or the
        series has no value at the end or the start of a requested window.
    """
    _check_window(window)
    ends = (
        window_ends(window, positions[-1] if positions else 0.0)
        if at is None
        else list(at)
    )

    totals = []
    for end in ends:
        start = end - window
        if start < -POSITION_TOLERANCE * max(abs(end), 1.0):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Position {end} has no complete window of {window} before it."
            )
        totals.append(
            series[index_at(positions, end)]
            - series[index_at(positions, max(start, 0.0))]
        )
    return totals

Draws of the parameters of a calibration problem, each with a weight.

A method that has draws returns them in a sample: a bootstrap, a sequential Monte Carlo run, a Markov chain. Plots, reports, the predictive and the scores read a sample, never the result of one method. Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust; with equal weights it is the unweighted statistic.

A sample has no single set of parameters: to run one draw, take it from draws.

The natural logarithm of each draw's weight, normalized so that the weights sum to 1. A draw of weight zero has -inf.

class ParameterSample(BaseModel):
    """
    Draws of the parameters of a calibration problem, each with a weight.

    A method that has draws returns them in a sample: a bootstrap, a
    sequential Monte Carlo run, a Markov chain. Plots, reports, the
    predictive and the scores read a sample, never the result of one method.
    Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust; with equal weights it
    is the unweighted statistic.

    A sample has no single set of parameters: to run one draw, take it from
    `draws`.

    Attributes
    ----------
    names : list[str]
        One name per column, in the order of the problem's parameters.
    bounds : list[tuple[float, float]]
        The bounds of each parameter; every value lies inside them.
    values : list[list[float]]
        One row per draw, one column per name.
    log_weights : list[float]
        The natural logarithm of each draw's weight, normalized so that the
        weights sum to 1. A draw of weight zero has ``-inf``.
    groups : list[int] | None
        The group of each draw (a chain, a replicate or a wave), or None.
    method : SampleMethod
        What made the sample.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a value is not finite or outside its bounds, a log weight is NaN or
        ``+inf``, every log weight is ``-inf``, a name repeats, or the shapes
        differ.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid", frozen=True, ser_json_inf_nan="constants")

    names: list[str] = Field(description="One name per column.")
    bounds: list[tuple[float, float]] = Field(description="Bounds of each parameter.")
    values: list[list[float]] = Field(description="One row per draw.")
    log_weights: list[float] = Field(description="Normalized log weight of each draw.")
    groups: list[int] | None = Field(default=None, description="Group of each draw.")
    method: SampleMethod = Field(description="What made the sample.")

    _rust: "ParameterSampleProtocol" = PrivateAttr()

    @model_validator(mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def normalize_log_weights(cls, data: object) -> object:
        """Check the invariants in Rust and normalize the log weights."""
        if not isinstance(data, Mapping):
            return data
        rust = commol_rs.inference.ParameterSample(
            list(data.get("names", [])),
            [tuple(bound) for bound in data.get("bounds", [])],
            [list(row) for row in data.get("values", [])],
            [float(w) for w in data.get("log_weights", [])],
            data.get("groups"),
        )
        return {**data, "log_weights": rust.log_weights}

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def build_rust_sample(self) -> Self:
        """Keep the Rust sample that computes the statistics."""
        self._rust = commol_rs.inference.ParameterSample(
            self.names, self.bounds, self.values, self.log_weights, self.groups
        )
        return self

    def __eq__(self, other: object) -> bool:
        """Two samples are equal when their fields are."""
        if not isinstance(other, ParameterSample):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.model_dump() == other.model_dump()

    __hash__ = None  # type: ignore[assignment]

    @classmethod
    def equally_weighted(
        cls,
        names: list[str],
        bounds: list[tuple[float, float]],
        values: list[list[float]],
        method: SampleMethod,
        groups: list[int] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """
        A sample whose draws have equal weights.

        Parameters
        ----------
        names : list[str]
            One name per column.
        bounds : list[tuple[float, float]]
            The bounds of each parameter.
        values : list[list[float]]
            One row per draw.
        method : SampleMethod
            What made the sample.
        groups : list[int] | None, optional
            The group of each draw.

        Returns
        -------
        ParameterSample
            The sample.
        """
        return cls(
            names=names,
            bounds=bounds,
            values=values,
            log_weights=[0.0] * len(values),
            groups=groups,
            method=method,
        )

    @property
    def rust_sample(self) -> "ParameterSampleProtocol":
        """The sample in Rust, for the runners of methods and the predictive."""
        return self._rust

    @property
    def weights(self) -> list[float]:
        """The weight of each draw; they sum to 1."""
        return self._rust.weights

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        """The number of draws."""
        return len(self.values)

    def draws(self) -> Iterator[dict[str, float]]:
        """
        Every draw, as a mapping of parameter name to value.

        Yields
        ------
        dict[str, float]
            One draw, in the order of `values`.
        """
        for row in self.values:
            yield dict(zip(self.names, row, strict=True))

    def mean(self) -> dict[str, float]:
        """
        The weighted mean of each parameter.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, float]
            One mean per name.
        """
        return dict(zip(self.names, self._rust.mean(), strict=True))

    def covariance(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        The weighted covariance matrix, in the order of `names`.

        With weights ``w`` that sum to 1 it is
        ``Σ wᵢ(xᵢ − x̄)(yᵢ − ȳ) / (1 − Σ wᵢ²)``: with equal weights, the
        sample covariance. It is NaN for a sample of one effective draw.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            One row per name.
        """
        return self._rust.covariance()

    def correlation(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """
        The weighted correlation matrix, in the order of `names`.

        Returns
        -------
        list[list[float]]
            One row per name; NaN for a parameter with no spread.
        """
        return self._rust.correlation()

    def quantiles(self, levels: list[float]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        """
        The weighted quantiles of each parameter.

        The quantile is the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution,
        interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights; with
        equal weights it is NumPy's ``method="hazen"``.

        Parameters
        ----------
        levels : list[float]
            Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, list[float]]
            One quantile per level for each name.
        """
        rows = self._rust.quantiles([float(level) for level in levels])
        return {
            name: [row[column] for row in rows]
            for column, name in enumerate(self.names)
        }

    def interval(self, confidence_level: float) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
        """
        The central interval of each parameter.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1, such as 0.95.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, tuple[float, float]]
            ``(lower, upper)`` for each name: the quantiles
            ``(1 − c)/2`` and ``(1 + c)/2``.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        lower, upper = self._rust.interval(confidence_level)
        return {
            name: (low, high)
            for name, low, high in zip(self.names, lower, upper, strict=True)
        }

    def effective_size(self) -> float:
        """
        Kish's effective sample size: ``1 / Σ wᵢ²``.

        Returns
        -------
        float
            Between 1 and the number of draws; equal weights give the number
            of draws.
        """
        return self._rust.effective_size()

    def resample(self, count: int, seed: int) -> "ParameterSample":
        """
        Draw `count` draws with replacement, each with probability its weight.

        Parameters
        ----------
        count : int
            Number of draws.
        seed : int
            Seed of the generator.

        Returns
        -------
        ParameterSample
            A sample of equal weights.
        """
        indices = self._rust.resample(count, seed)
        return ParameterSample.equally_weighted(
            self.names,
            self.bounds,
            [self.values[i] for i in indices],
            SampleMethod(
                name="resample",
                settings={"of": self.method.name, "count": count, "seed": seed},
            ),
        )

    def summary(self, confidence_level: float) -> dict[str, ParameterSummary]:
        """
        Weighted statistics of each parameter, for a report.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        dict[str, ParameterSummary]
            One summary per name.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        lower, upper = self._rust.interval(confidence_level)
        quantiles = self.quantiles([0.0, 0.5, 1.0])
        mean = self.mean()
        covariance = self.covariance()
        return {
            name: ParameterSummary(
                mean=mean[name],
                median=quantiles[name][1],
                std=covariance[index][index] ** 0.5,
                lower=lower[index],
                upper=upper[index],
                min=quantiles[name][0],
                max=quantiles[name][2],
            )
            for index, name in enumerate(self.names)
        }

def normalize_log_weights(cls, data: object) -> object:

    rust = commol_rs.inference.ParameterSample(

The draws run in parallel in Rust, through the forward model of the calibration problem: with a stochastic engine every replicate of a draw is a draw of the predictive, with an equal share of its weight. Source code in commol/api/inference/predictive.py 
class Predictive:
    """
    The run of every draw of a parameter sample.

    The draws run in parallel in Rust, through the forward model of the
    calibration problem: with a stochastic engine every replicate of a draw is
    a draw of the predictive, with an equal share of its weight. A band
    reduces the draws position by position with their weights; without
    observation noise it is a band of the model, not a prediction interval.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        calibrator: "Calibrator",
        sample: ParameterSample,
        positions: Sequence[float],
    ):
        """
        Run every draw of `sample` at `positions`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        calibrator : Calibrator
            The calibration problem the sample is a sample of.
        sample : ParameterSample
            Its parameters, in the problem's order.
        positions : Sequence[float]
            Positions to report at, ascending.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the sample's parameters are not the problem's.
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a draw leaves the values its model allows.
        """
        self.calibrator: "Calibrator" = calibrator
        self.sample: ParameterSample = sample
        self.positions: list[float] = [float(position) for position in positions]
        self.output_names: list[str] = list(calibrator.simulation.engine.output_names)
        self._rust = calibrator.rust_problem.predictive(
            sample.rust_sample, self.positions
        )

    @property
    def weights(self) -> list[float]:
        """The weight of each draw of the predictive; they sum to 1."""
        return self._rust.weights

    def runs(self) -> list[SimulationResults]:
        """
        The trajectory of every draw, in the order of `weights`.

        Returns
        -------
        list[SimulationResults]
            One run per draw, at `positions`.
        """
        return [
            SimulationResults.from_rows(self.positions, self.output_names, rows)
            for rows in self._rust.trajectories
        ]

    def band(self, confidence_level: float) -> PredictiveBand:
        """
        The band of every output.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        PredictiveBand
            The weighted mean, median and central interval of each output at
            each position.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.band(confidence_level)

        def by_output(table: list[list[float]]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
            return {
                name: [row[index] for row in table]
                for index, name in enumerate(self.output_names)
            }

        return PredictiveBand(
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            positions=self.positions,
            mean=by_output(mean),
            median=by_output(median),
            lower=by_output(lower),
            upper=by_output(upper),
        )

    def series_band(
        self,
        outputs: Sequence[str],
        confidence_level: float,
        cumulative: bool = False,
    ) -> SeriesBand:
        """
        The band of the sum of some outputs, or of its running total.

        Each draw is reduced to the series first, then the series are reduced
        across the draws.

        Parameters
        ----------
        outputs : Sequence[str]
            The outputs summed.
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.
        cumulative : bool, optional
            Whether the series is the running total along the positions.

        Returns
        -------
        SeriesBand
            One value per position.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an output is unknown or the confidence level is out of range.
        """
        unknown = [name for name in outputs if name not in self.output_names]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown outputs {unknown}. Outputs: {self.output_names}."
            )
        indices = [self.output_names.index(name) for name in outputs]
        mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.series_band(
            indices, cumulative, confidence_level
        )
        return SeriesBand(
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            positions=self.positions,
            mean=mean,
            median=median,
            lower=lower,
            upper=upper,
        )

    def at_observations(
        self, observed_data: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
    ) -> ObservationDraws:
        """
        Every draw's value of each observation.

        The observations need not be the ones the problem was fitted to: held
        out data are read the same way, through the observation operator.

        Parameters
        ----------
        observed_data : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations.

        Returns
        -------
        ObservationDraws
            Each draw's value of each observation.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If an observation names an unknown output or factor.
        InfeasibleStateError
            If a draw leaves the values its model allows.
        """
        draws = self.calibrator.rust_problem.observation_draws(
            self.sample.rust_sample,
            engine_state.rust_observed_data(list(observed_data)),
        )
        return ObservationDraws(observed_data, draws)

    Parameters
    ----------
    calibrator : Calibrator
        The calibration problem the sample is a sample of.
    sample : ParameterSample
        Its parameters, in the problem's order.
    positions : Sequence[float]
        Positions to report at, ascending.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the sample's parameters are not the problem's.
    InfeasibleStateError
        If a draw leaves the values its model allows.
    """
    self.calibrator: "Calibrator" = calibrator
    self.sample: ParameterSample = sample
    self.positions: list[float] = [float(position) for position in positions]
    self.output_names: list[str] = list(calibrator.simulation.engine.output_names)
    self._rust = calibrator.rust_problem.predictive(
        sample.rust_sample, self.positions
    )

def band(self, confidence_level: float) -> PredictiveBand:
    """
    The band of every output.

    Parameters
    ----------
    confidence_level : float
        Strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    PredictiveBand
        The weighted mean, median and central interval of each output at
        each position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
    """
    mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.band(confidence_level)

    def by_output(table: list[list[float]]) -> dict[str, list[float]]:
        return {
            name: [row[index] for row in table]
            for index, name in enumerate(self.output_names)
        }

    return PredictiveBand(
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        positions=self.positions,
        mean=by_output(mean),
        median=by_output(median),
        lower=by_output(lower),
        upper=by_output(upper),
    )

def series_band(
    self,
    outputs: Sequence[str],
    confidence_level: float,
    cumulative: bool = False,
) -> SeriesBand:
    """
    The band of the sum of some outputs, or of its running total.

    Each draw is reduced to the series first, then the series are reduced
    across the draws.

    Parameters
    ----------
    outputs : Sequence[str]
        The outputs summed.
    confidence_level : float
        Strictly between 0 and 1.
    cumulative : bool, optional
        Whether the series is the running total along the positions.

    Returns
    -------
    SeriesBand
        One value per position.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If an output is unknown or the confidence level is out of range.
    """
    unknown = [name for name in outputs if name not in self.output_names]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown outputs {unknown}. Outputs: {self.output_names}."
        )
    indices = [self.output_names.index(name) for name in outputs]
    mean, median, lower, upper = self._rust.series_band(
        indices, cumulative, confidence_level
    )
    return SeriesBand(
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        positions=self.positions,
        mean=mean,
        median=median,
        lower=lower,
        upper=upper,
    )

class ObservationDraws:
    """
    Every draw's value of a set of observations.

    The values are read through the observation operator of the calibration
    problem (sums of outputs, windows, factors), the one the loss uses. Without
    observation noise their interval is a band of the model, not a prediction
    interval.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
        draws: "ObservationDrawsProtocol",
    ):
        """
        Wrap the draws of `observations`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        observations : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
            The observations, in the order of each draw's values.
        draws : ObservationDrawsProtocol
            The draws, computed in Rust.
        """
        self.observations: list[ObservedDataPoint] = list(observations)
        self.rust_draws: "ObservationDrawsProtocol" = draws

    @property
    def values(self) -> list[list[float]]:
        """Each draw's value of each observation, ``[draw][observation]``."""
        return self.rust_draws.values

    @property
    def weights(self) -> list[float]:
        """The weight of each draw; they sum to 1."""
        return self.rust_draws.weights

    @property
    def observed(self) -> list[float]:
        """The observed value of each observation."""
        return [point.value for point in self.observations]

    def band(self, confidence_level: float) -> SeriesBand:
        """
        The band of each observation across the draws.

        Parameters
        ----------
        confidence_level : float
            Strictly between 0 and 1.

        Returns
        -------
        SeriesBand
            One value per observation, at its position.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the confidence level is not strictly between 0 and 1.
        """
        mean, median, lower, upper = self.rust_draws.band(confidence_level)
        return SeriesBand(
            confidence_level=confidence_level,
            positions=[point.at for point in self.observations],
            mean=mean,
            median=median,
            lower=lower,
            upper=upper,
        )

def weighted_interval_score(
    predictive: Predictive,
    observations: Sequence[ObservedDataPoint],
    confidence_levels: Sequence[float],
) -> Score:
    """
    The weighted interval score of Bracher et al. (2021).

    ``(½|y − m| + Σₖ (αₖ/2) IS_αₖ) / (K + ½)``, with ``m`` the median and
    ``αₖ = 1 − cₖ`` for each confidence level ``cₖ``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    predictive : Predictive
        The predictive.
    observations : Sequence[ObservedDataPoint]
        The observations to score.
    confidence_levels : Sequence[float]
        The levels of the central intervals.

    Returns
    -------
    Score
        Lower is better.

    References
    ----------
    Bracher, J., Ray, E. L., Gneiting, T., & Reich, N. G. (2021). Evaluating
    epidemic forecasts in an interval format. PLOS Computational Biology,
    17(2), e1008618. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008618
    """
    draws = predictive.at_observations(observations)
    return _score(
        draws,
        draws.rust_draws.weighted_interval_score(
            draws.observed, [float(c) for c in confidence_levels]
        ),
    )

def weighted_quantiles(
    values: Sequence[float],
    levels: Sequence[float],
    weights: Sequence[float] | None = None,
) -> list[float]:
    """
    Quantiles of weighted values, by the one convention of commol.

    The quantile is the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution,
    interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights. With equal
    weights it equals ``numpy.percentile(..., method="hazen")``. A weight of
    zero removes a value.

    Parameters
    ----------
    values : Sequence[float]
        The values.
    levels : Sequence[float]
        Quantile levels, each between 0 and 1.
    weights : Sequence[float] | None, optional
        One non-negative weight per value, of any scale. None gives equal
        weights.

    Returns
    -------
    list[float]
        One quantile per level.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the lengths differ or no weight is positive.
    """
    values = [float(value) for value in values]
    if weights is None:
        weights = [1.0] * len(values)
    return commol_rs.inference.weighted_quantiles(
        values, [float(w) for w in weights], [float(level) for level in levels]
    )

        Confidence level of the reported interval, strictly between 0 and 1.
    weights : Sequence[float] | None, optional
        One weight per member, such as the weights of a
        :class:`~commol.Predictive`. None gives equal weights.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float] | dict[str, list[float]]
        Keys ``mean``, ``median``, ``ci_lower``, ``ci_upper``, ``min`` and
        ``max``. Scalar members give scalar statistics, series members give
        series statistics. ``min`` and ``max`` are over the members of
        positive weight.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is out of range, ``per_member`` is empty, or
        the weights do not match the members.
    """
    lower_point, upper_point = ci_percentiles(confidence_level)
    values = np.asarray(per_member, dtype=float)
    if values.size == 0:
        raise ValueError("per_member must hold at least one ensemble member.")
    member_weights = (
        [1.0] * values.shape[0] if weights is None else [float(w) for w in weights]
    )
    if len(member_weights) != values.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"One weight per member: {values.shape[0]} members, "
            f"{len(member_weights)} weights."
        )
    levels = [0.0, lower_point / 100.0, 0.5, upper_point / 100.0, 1.0]
    columns = values.reshape(values.shape[0], -1).T
    table = [
        weighted_quantiles(column.tolist(), levels, member_weights)
        for column in columns
    ]
    means = [
        commol_rs.inference.weighted_mean(column.tolist(), member_weights)
        for column in columns
    ]

    def shaped(per_column: list[float]) -> float | list[float]:
        return per_column[0] if values.ndim == 1 else per_column

    return {
        "mean": shaped(means),
        "median": shaped([row[2] for row in table]),
        "ci_lower": shaped([row[1] for row in table]),
        "ci_upper": shaped([row[3] for row in table]),
        "min": shaped([row[0] for row in table]),
        "max": shaped([row[4] for row in table]),
    }

def ci_percentiles(confidence_level: float) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """
    Lower and upper percentile points of a two-sided confidence interval.

    Parameters
    ----------
    confidence_level : float
        Confidence level of the interval, strictly between 0 and 1.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[float, float]
        Lower and upper percentile points, on the 0-100 scale.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``confidence_level`` is not strictly between 0 and 1.
    """
    if not 0.0 < confidence_level < 1.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"confidence_level must be strictly between 0 and 1, got "
            f"{confidence_level}. Note this is a fraction, not a percentage: "
            f"use 0.95 for a 95% interval."
        )
    return (
        (1.0 - confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
        (1.0 + confidence_level) / 2.0 * 100.0,
    )

def register(
    method_type: type[MethodT],
    runner: Callable[["Calibrator", MethodT], BaseModel],
) -> None:
    """
    Register the runner of an inference method.

    Parameters
    ----------
    method_type : type[InferenceMethod]
        The configuration type of the method.
    runner : Callable[[Calibrator, InferenceMethod], BaseModel]
        Runs the method on a calibrator and returns its result.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the type already has a runner.
    """
    if method_type in _RUNNERS:
        raise ValueError(f"{method_type.__name__} already has a runner.")
    _RUNNERS[method_type] = cast("Runner", runner)

def run_method(
    calibrator: "Calibrator",
    method: InferenceMethod[ResultT],
    kind: type[InferenceMethod[BaseModel]],
) -> ResultT:
    """
    Run `method` on `calibrator` with the runner of its type.

    Parameters
    ----------
    calibrator : Calibrator
        The calibration problem.
    method : InferenceMethod[ResultT]
        The configuration of the method.
    kind : type[InferenceMethod]
        The kind of method the entry point takes: `UncertaintyMethod` or
        `IdentifiabilityMethod`.

    Returns
    -------
    ResultT
        The method's result.

    Raises
    ------
    TypeError
        If `method` is not of `kind`; the message names its entry point.
    ValueError
        If no runner is registered for the configuration's type.
    """
    if not isinstance(method, kind):
        right = next(
            (
                name
                for other, name in _ENTRY_POINTS.items()
                if isinstance(method, other)
            ),
            None,
        )
        hint = f" Run it with {right}." if right else ""
        raise TypeError(f"{type(method).__name__} is not a {kind.__name__}.{hint}")
    runner = _RUNNERS.get(type(method))
    if runner is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"No method is registered for {type(method).__name__}. "
            f"Registered: {registered()}."
        )
    return cast("ResultT", runner(calibrator, method))

docs.text:
Back to Home

This guide helps you find the right code before you change Commol. It is an index for maintainers and AI agents, not an API reference: for the public API, see the User Guide and the API Reference.

These pages describe main

The dev version of this site is built from main and may describe unreleased code. The latest version is built from the last release tag.

docs.title: Who this is for

docs.title: 90-second mental model
docs.text:
Commol has three layers (Architecture draws them). The user writes a model in Python. Python validates it and serializes it to JSON. The Rust engine builds and runs it.

User code
  |
  v
py-commol/commol/api/        ModelBuilder, Simulation, Calibrator, reports
  |
  v
py-commol/commol/context/    Pydantic model: validation and serialization
  |
  |  Model.model_dump_json()
  v
py-commol/src/               PyO3 bindings (module commol.commol_rs._commol_rs)
  |
  v
crates/commol-core/          model types, expressions (Cranelift JIT), SimulationEngine trait
crates/commol-model/         expansion, initial state, flow planning, rates, derivatives
crates/commol-difference/    the discrete step: X += derivatives
crates/commol-differential/  the ODE engine: diffsol integrates derivatives
crates/commol-calibration/   the problem in layers, optimizers (argmin fork), starts
crates/commol-inference/     parameter sample, predictive, scores, quantiles

Golden rule: the Rust engine is the single source of truth. When Python needs to know how the engine expands, initializes, plans or simulates a model, it asks the engine through a binding. It never re-implements the rule.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

This page shows how the code of Commol is put together, in three diagrams. It is for a person who wants the big picture before reading files. For the rules behind the picture, read the Mental model; to find the file that owns a behavior, read the Repository map.

docs.title: The big picture
docs.text:
Commol has two halves. Python is the front: the user writes the model there, and sees the results there. Rust is the back: it turns the model into numbers.

flowchart TB
    U([User script])
    API["Python: api/<br/>ModelBuilder, Simulation, Calibrator"]
    CTX["Python: context/<br/>Model: validated data"]
    BR["Bridge: py-commol/src<br/>PyO3 module commol_rs"]
    RS["Rust: crates/<br/>compiler, engines, calibration, inference"]
    U --> API
    API --> CTX
    CTX -->|model as JSON| BR
    BR --> RS
    RS -.->|results| API
Half Folder Job Python py-commol/commol/ The public API (api/) and the model as validated data (context/). Bridge py-commol/src/ Exposes the Rust functions to Python (PyO3). Rust crates/ Every rule about how a model becomes numbers, how it is calibrated, and how the uncertainty of a calibration is measured.

Golden rule: Python never computes how a model expands or runs. It asks Rust.

docs.title: Inside Rust
docs.text:
One compiler reads the model. Each engine runs the compiled model with its own method and gives one series per output. Calibration runs an engine many times and compares the series with the observations. Inference reads the calibration problem to measure uncertainty. The arrows show this flow, from top to bottom. The dashed box is the base that every box uses.

flowchart TB
    J[/model as JSON/]
    M["Model compiler<br/>compartments, initial state,<br/>flows, rates"]
    E1["Difference<br/>one step at a time"]
    E2["Differential<br/>ODE solver"]
    E3["Stochastic<br/>random events"]
    O[/one series per output/]
    C["Calibration<br/>the problem in layers, optimizers"]
    I["Inference<br/>parameter sample, predictive, scores,<br/>sensitivities, identifiability"]
    F["Base: commol-core, commol-random<br/>used by every box"]
    J --> M
    M --> E1 & E2 & E3
    E1 & E2 & E3 --> O
    O --> C
    C --> I
    I ~~~ F
    classDef base stroke-dasharray: 5 5
    class F base
Box Crate Job Model compiler commol-model Expands the model into compartments, builds the initial state, plans the flows and compiles the rates. Difference commol-difference Adds the change of each step: X += derivatives. Differential commol-differential Integrates the ODEs with diffsol. Stochastic commol-stochastic Moves whole units by random events. Calibration commol-calibration The calibration problem in layers (forward model, observation operator, feasibility, discrepancy, optimization objective), and the optimizers that find the values that make an engine match observations, from one or several starts. Inference commol-inference What every uncertainty method returns or reads: the weighted parameter sample, the one quantile, the predictive of a sample and its scores; the port of sensitivities and the identifiability analyses. It depends on calibration, never the reverse.

Every box uses commol-core (shared types, rate formulas, the SimulationEngine trait). The stochastic engines and calibration also use commol-random (random numbers), and so does inference. Calibration works through the SimulationEngine trait, so it does not depend on a specific engine; inference reaches an engine only through the forward model of a calibration problem.

docs.title: The path of a simulation and a calibration
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    A[ModelBuilder] -->|build| B[Model]
    B --> S[Simulation]
    S -->|model as JSON, once| K[Rust: compile the model]
    K --> R[Rust: run the engine]
    R --> SR[SimulationResults]
    K --> CAL[Calibrator]
    CAL -->|problem, once| P[Rust: calibration problem]
    P --> L[Rust: optimizer loop, one or more starts]
    L --> CR[CalibrationResult]
    CR -.->|apply_calibration_parameters| B
    P --> U[Rust: uncertainty method]
    U --> PS[ParameterSample]
    PS --> PR[Predictive: bands, scores]
  1. ModelBuilder (api/model_builder.py) collects the model, and build returns a validated Model (context/model.py).
  2. Simulation (api/simulation.py) sends the model to Rust once, through build_engine (context/_model/engine_state.py). Rust compiles it.

  3. Each run calls the Rust engine and returns SimulationResults (api/results.py).

  4. Calibrator (api/calibrator.py) takes the compiled engine of a Simulation and builds the calibration problem in Rust once (commol_rs.inference.CalibrationProblem, py-commol/src/inference.rs). run(starts=n) runs the optimizer loop in Rust from each start and returns the best CalibrationResult.

  5. apply_calibration_parameters writes the result back into the Model.
  6. Calibrator.uncertainty(method) runs a method on the same problem. A method with draws returns a ParameterSample; a Predictive (api/inference/predictive.py) runs its draws, and commol.scores checks them against observations.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

How code, comments, documentation and commits are written in Commol. The tools check some of these rules. The rest depend on the author and the reviewer.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Area Rule Checked by Python style Ruff, line length 88 ruff check, ruff format (pre-commit, CI) Python types Annotations on every signature; never Any ty check (pre-commit, CI) Python dead code No unused code; a name used only in a string annotation goes in py-commol/.vulture_allowlist.py vulture (pre-commit, CI) Rust style cargo fmt; no Clippy warnings pre-commit, CI (-D warnings) Rust docs Every public item documented (missing_docs); no broken doc links clippy and cargo doc (CI) Docstrings NumPy style on every public module, class, function and argument ruff rules D1 and D417 (pre-commit, CI) Comments Describe the code as it is Review Documentation Mandatory with every change: definition of done CI and review Doc examples Abstract names; every block runs pytest -m docs (CI) and review Tests One package per guide page; shared factories; every test checks a result Review; pytest 10 deprecations fail the run (filterwarnings) Commits type(scope): description Review

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
• Every function and method signature has type hints. Never use Any: use a precise type, a TypeVar, a Protocol or a union.
  • Public functions and methods have a NumPy-style docstring: a one-line summary, then Parameters, Returns and Raises as needed. Private helpers may use a one-line docstring.
  • Context data structures are Pydantic v2 models.
  • ModelBuilder methods return Self, so calls chain.
  • Log with the standard logging module. Library code never writes to the standard error of the process: a failure is part of the result and the caller logs it (CalibrationResult.failed_runs). Output the user asks for, such as a verbose optimizer's table, goes to Python's sys.stdout.

docs.title: Rust
docs.text:
• Edition 2024.
  • Public items have rustdoc comments, and a new module starts with a //! summary.
  • Hot paths avoid allocation: reuse buffers, access by index, keep evaluation contexts alive.
  • No println! or eprintln! in library code: return the information to the caller.

docs.title: Comments and docstrings
docs.text:
Describe the code as it is now. Never describe how it came to be.

Do not write Write instead "This replaces the old prefix matching" "Matches compartments by label." "Previously this was computed in Python" Nothing: the history is in git. "This is what makes calibration work" The rule the caller must satisfy. "Kept in sync with builder.rs" A test that fails when they differ.

Design reasons and invariants that cross components go to Design decisions, not to the source.

docs.title: Documentation definition of done
docs.text:
Mandatory

Every change to this repository ships with the documentation it needs, in the agreed format and at the agreed quality. A change without it is not done, and its pull request is not merged. This applies to people and to agents, to features, fixes, refactors, dependency updates and CI changes.

docs.title: 1. Update the docs the change affects
docs.text:
If the change… Update Adds or changes a public Python name, argument, default or error Its docstring; a path entry in docs/api/ for a new name in commol.__all__; the guide page that uses it Changes model behavior (expansion, rates, initial conditions, simulation) The guide page in docs/guide/; Model structure if a type changes Changes calibration or uncertainty guide/calibration.md and its sub-pages, or guide/uncertainty/ Changes an expression function or variable guide/mathematical-expressions.md Moves code, adds a module, or changes who owns what Repository map; AGENTS.md if a "If you need to…" row changes Adds or removes a crate, an engine or a layer, or changes the path of a simulation or a calibration The diagrams and tables of Architecture Adds or changes a rule that is not obvious from the code Design decisions, with the test that guards it Changes a workflow, a command, CI or the release AGENTS.md; docs/development/ Plans new work An issue from a template of .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ (Planning) Is visible to users docs/about/changelog.md, under [Unreleased] Adds or changes a public Rust item Its rustdoc comment

When in doubt, search docs/ and AGENTS.md for the changed name and update every match.

docs.title: 2. Use the agreed format
docs.text:
Pages

  • One page, one job. The title says the outcome.
  • Start with one paragraph (what it is, who it is for), then a quick path, then details, then a checklist or the next step.
  • Prefer tables, checklists and short sections to long prose.
  • Start every page with a link back to its index, and end it with previous/next links when it belongs to a sequence.

Text

  • Simple technical English: short sentences, one idea per sentence, active voice, the answer first.
  • Every claim about the code names the file, function or test behind it.
  • Describe the present. History belongs in git and in the changelog.

Examples

  • Use abstract names only: bins A, B, C; categories group1, cat1; parameters k1, alpha. No names from epidemiology, chemistry or any other field.
  • Every Python block runs, top to bottom within its page, in one namespace and from a temporary directory (py-commol/tests/docs/test_examples.py). Define what a block needs in an earlier block of the same page.

  • A block that cannot run alone (a signature, a fragment) is marked on the line just before its fence, with a reason:

    <!-- doc-test: skip: shows only the signature -->

Use the marker only when the block cannot run; never to hide a failing example.

Code documentation

  • Python: a NumPy-style docstring on every public function, method and class (Parameters, Returns, Raises).
  • Rust: a rustdoc comment on every public item; a //! summary at the top of every new module.
  • Comments follow Comments and docstrings.

docs.title: 3. Pass the quality checks
docs.text:
Check Command Enforced by The site builds with no broken internal link or anchor mkdocs build --strict (with validation: in mkdocs.yaml) CI (Documentation) External links answer lychee (.github/workflows/links.yaml) CI on documentation changes, weekly; not a required check The documentation examples run pytest -m docs (from py-commol/) CI (Code Quality) Every name in commol.__all__ has an API entry (… under docs/api/) pytest -m docs (tests/docs/test_reference.py) CI (Code Quality) Every crate under crates/ is named in Architecture pytest -m docs (tests/docs/test_reference.py) CI (Code Quality) Public Python modules, classes, functions and arguments have docstrings ruff check . (rules D1, D417, NumPy convention) pre-commit, CI Public Rust items have docs, without broken links #![warn(missing_docs)] in every crate (denied by clippy -D warnings); RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc pre-commit (clippy), CI The table in step 1 is complete for this change — Pull request checklist and review The format in step 2 is followed — Review

The pull request template repeats this checklist. A reviewer who finds a gap asks for it before approving.

docs.title: Writing for people and agents
docs.text:
The same pages serve both. An agent reads the Markdown source by path, so:

  • keep each page self-contained, with its links;
  • name files and functions exactly, in code format;
  • put the rule before the explanation.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Where a Python test goes, how it builds its model, and what it must check. The tests live in py-commol/tests/.

docs.title: Layout: one package per guide page
docs.text:
A test goes in the package of the guide page that documents the behavior it checks, so "where is the test of X" has the same answer as "where is the guide of X". A pure-Python helper (utils/security.py, context/axis_units.py, api/inference/intervals.py) goes in the package of its feature. The exceptions are reference_models/, which checks published models across features (see Reference models), and model_kinds/, which runs a model kind that is not aggregate through every generic layer.

Package Tests of Guide page building/ The builder, parameters, stratifications, reserved names, save and load Building Models transitions/ Flows, $compartment, stratified rates, impulses Transitions rates/ Formulas, functions, variables, expression security Mathematical Expressions axis_patterns/ AxisPattern formulas, runs and schedules Axis Patterns initial_conditions/ Bin, stratification and compartment fractions; the initial state Building Models simulation/ Runs, run_at, results and their positions, differential models, outputs, the window grid and windowed totals, AxisUnits Running Simulations stochastic/ The stochastic engines of an aggregate model through the layers: their means against the deterministic engines, whole units, calibration with replicates (the closed forms are in crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs) Stochastic Simulation units/ Unit checks Units description/ Model.describe, its sections and blocks, the renderers and their snapshots (description/snapshots/), the equations of the dynamics (equation_forms in support/description.py) Describing a Model calibration/ One file per calibration page: test_problem.py, test_optimizers.py, test_starts.py, test_constraints.py, test_observations.py, test_initial_conditions.py, test_write_back.py Model Calibration and its sub-pages uncertainty/ The parameter sample, the one quantile, the predictive, the scores, the entry point Calibrator.uncertainty, and the coverage harness (test_coverage.py, marker coverage_study) Uncertainty reporting/ Reports Reports plotting/ SimulationPlotter Running Simulations docs/ The documentation examples and the API coverage (marker docs) — reference_models/ Published models against their stated results, one module per model family — (across features) model_kinds/ The test model kind (support/kinds.py) through a simulation, a calibration, a report and a plot; the check that an engine runs its kind; the variants of a structure (UnstratifiedVariant). It needs the extension built with --features test-kind. — (across features; Design decisions) support/ No tests: the code the tests share —

Keep a test module under about 600 lines. When it grows past that, split it by topic inside its package.

docs.title: Models: use the factories
docs.text:
• Build models with the factories of tests/support/models.py: abc_builder (A → B → C), abcd_builder (A → B → C → D) and a_to_b_builder, and the special models override_builder, shared_category_builder and conditional_pathway_builder. A factory returns a FactoryBuilder: a ModelBuilder of the process and the Aggregate that lays it out (builder.structure, which set_structure replaces). A keyword overrides one part of the default model, so a test names only what it changes. build builds for difference equations; build_ode builds for differential equations, with the tight solver settings TIGHT by default; build_stochastic builds for a stochastic engine (STOCHASTIC_ENGINES, and MEAN_FIELD, the deterministic engine of each); run builds and simulates.
  • Build a model by hand only when one test needs it and no factory keyword expresses it. A model that a second file needs goes to support/.
  • Test models use abstract names, as examples do: bins A, B, C, parameters k1, k2, categories g1, t1. Only tests/reference_models/ and the support code that only it uses (support/oracles.py, support/flows.py) keep the names of their published source.
  • Fixtures: abc_model and abc_simulation (tests/conftest.py); truth and truth_run (tests/calibration/conftest.py). A fixture is function-scoped unless its cost is measured; a wider scope never holds an object a test can change. A class-scoped fixture is never an instance method (removed in pytest 10).

docs.title: Every test checks a result
docs.text:
A test compares a result with an oracle:

Oracle Example A value computed by hand in the test reference_run (tests/support/reference.py) evaluates the flows in plain Python, as the engine does: every flow from the state at the start of the step, no clamping. tests/rates/test_formulas.py compares whole trajectories with it. An analytic value An outflow rate d on every bin gives total(t) = total(0) (1 - d)^t (tests/transitions/test_compartment_placeholder.py). An invariant A total that the model keeps (assert_total_conserved); two paths that must agree, such as a bin id and the explicit sum of its compartments. What a stated result predicts about a run tests/support/oracles.py, for the reference models: final_size solves the final size relation, assert_threshold checks that a model grows at a reproduction number of 1.05 and decays at 0.95, settled reads a limit once doubling the horizon no longer moves it.

"It runs" is not a result. A test whose only check is that no exception occurs is allowed only when the exception is its subject, such as a validator that accepts a valid input.

docs.title: Tolerances
docs.text:
• assert_close(actual, expected, rel=…, abs=…) (tests/support/assertions.py) needs a stated tolerance, and reports the key and the index of the first difference.
  • ENGINE_REL = 1e-9 compares the engine with a hand computation of the same arithmetic: only the order of the floating-point operations differs.
  • ODE_REL = 1e-6 compares a differential model with a closed form, a final size or an equilibrium. flow_model solves with FINE (TIGHT with atol = 1e-12), so the error of a value near zero stays below its own size.
  • pytest.approx with its default (relative 1e-6) suits a single value computed by hand.
  • An optimizer result states the tolerance its convergence allows, for example abs=1e-5 for Nelder-Mead on noise-free data.

docs.title: Reference models
docs.text:
tests/reference_models/ shows that commol can state published models and computes their stated results. A module holds one model family and is named after the published model (test_pulse_vaccination.py); a test checks one stated result (test_the_fixed_point_starts_the_periodic_orbit).

  • Attribution. The module docstring has a References section in the NumPy format with the original papers of the model and of its parameter values (authors, year, title, journal, DOI). A value or a result taken from a paper cites it in a comment next to the value. A model with no primary source is not added.
  • Independent oracle. The expected value comes from the stated result, computed with math or numpy: a closed form, a root of the final size relation, a spectral radius. A test never compares commol with commol. A quantity that commol does not output, such as a reproduction number, is checked through what it predicts about a run (tests/support/oracles.py).
  • Equations. To check that a model has the stated equations, increments reads its right-hand side at one state: a difference-equation step adds the flows of the state it starts from, and both engines compile the same flows.
  • Tolerances. ENGINE_REL for a discrete model, ODE_REL for a differential one; an asymptotic result is read with settled, and the test states its horizon.
  • Gaps. A model that commol cannot state, or computes wrong, gets a test marked xfail(strict=True, reason="F<n>: …") that names a finding of the task that added it, so a fix makes the test pass and forces the marker out.

To add a test, write the model with Flow and flow_model (tests/support/flows.py) from the initial value of each bin, compute the stated result in the test, and cite the papers.

docs.title: Commits
docs.text:
Use Conventional Commits: <type>(<scope>): <description>.

  • The scope is required.
  • The description is one short phrase, with no period.
  • No body, and no co-author or AI attribution lines.
  • Types: feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, perf, test, build, ci, chore.
feat(transitions): add rate patterns
fix(simulation): correct the total of a subgroup
docs(codebase): add repository map

See Development workflow for branches and merge methods.
