docs.title: Design Decisions
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

The rules on this page are not obvious from the code, and breaking one gives results that are wrong but look correct. Each rule names where it lives and the test that guards it. Read the ones of your area before you change it.

Area Decisions Model kinds One interface for every kind, a model by composition, neutral terms Model structure Compartments, what they hold, stratification order, outputs, variable names Transitions and rates Rate semantics, stratified rates, formula parameters, JIT cache Initial conditions Subgroup totals, calibrated values Time Physical units, step unit, time inside a step, impulses, windowed observations Engines One set of flows, seeds, whole units, solver Calibration Weights, Nelder-Mead bounds, simulations, one observation operator, constraints bound the support Uncertainty A sample carries its weights, one entry point Results Confidence intervals, descriptions, reports, model files Security Expressions

docs.title: One interface for every model kind
docs.text:
The layers that do not depend on how a model is built (Simulation, Calibrator, the uncertainty methods, the reports and SimulationPlotter) use only Model and the methods of ModelStructure (py-commol/commol/context/structure.py), and in Rust only the SimulationEngine trait (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs). What only an aggregate model has (compartments, initial fractions) is behind them: Aggregate (context/aggregate.py), and in Rust CompartmentalEngine and InitialConditionPlan (crates/commol-model/). A new kind, such as an agent network, is a new ModelStructure subclass with its engines in the list; nothing that exists changes.

Part Rule Why, against the alternative ModelStructure An abstract base class (Pydantic's metaclass derives from ABCMeta). A missing method fails when the object is made and names it; optional methods have a default. A typing.Protocol shows a missing method only under ty, or mid-run as an AttributeError, and gives no defaults. Engine kinds An engine names a method, not a kind: each entry of EngineType names the kinds it runs (EngineType::kinds). Model asks the list (check_kind) when it is made, and Engine::build asks it again and picks the implementation by the pair of the engine and the kind; the error names the engine, both kinds and the engines of the kind of the model (EngineType::engines_of). Without the check, a model of one kind reaches the engine of another and fails deep in its compilation. One engine per kind would multiply the names: a stochastic engine runs every structure that implements it. Values calibration sets parameter and factor are generic. Each kind declares the types of value of its own it accepts (ModelKind::value_types, which ModelStructure.calibration_value_types asks); the aggregate kind accepts initial_condition. The engine resolves and writes them (SimulationEngine::plan_values, apply_values). The calibration crate would know compartments, and a new kind could not calibrate values of its own without editing it. Report sections ModelStructure.report_sections adds the sections of a kind to applied_parameters_report (default: none); the aggregate kind adds initial_conditions. A check of the kind in reporting.py brings back a branch per kind. Expressions in constraints The engine names the values of an output row: output_names, state_outputs (their sum is total) and output_sums (a bin total, for an engine of the aggregate kind). The calibration would rebuild bin totals from compartment labels.

The test kind (tests/support/kinds.py, engine TestEngine in py-commol/src/test_kind.rs) is written only against the interface. The extension has it only when it is built with the cargo feature test-kind, as the tests and CI build it; a release build does not.

Guards: tests/model_kinds/ (a test model through a simulation, a calibration, a report and a plot; the kind check both ways; a process the test kind cannot run), crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_model_values.rs (the calibration with an engine that is not of the aggregate kind: values through plan_values and apply_values, constraints through output_sums and state_outputs), py-commol/src/engine.rs::an_engine_rejects_a_model_of_another_kind, crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs::an_engine_rejects_a_model_of_another_kind.

docs.title: A model is a header, a process, a structure and an engine
docs.text:
Model (Python context/model.py, Rust crates/commol-core/src/types/model.rs) is one class for every kind: name, description, version, step_unit, parameters, engine ({type, settings}), process and structure. The process (Process: bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions) is what changes and how, written once. The structure is what changes between kinds of model: Aggregate lays the process out as amounts per compartment; Network and Agents come with their proposals (#144, #145). It is tagged in JSON by kind. In Python Model is generic in its structure class: ModelBuilder.build(structure, engine) returns a Model of the class of structure (a TypeVar, never a value), so model.structure.total type-checks, and Model.from_json reads the class from the kind and variant of the file. The engine is part of the model because it sets what a rate means.

The interface of a kind stays on the structure and reads the process from the model (outputs_by_source(model), series_label(model, id)); the methods of Aggregate that need the bins take the process (initial_state(process)).

Alternative Why not Inheritance: an abstract Model with a CompartmentalModel Direct access (model.bins), but two parallel hierarchies, of models and of builders, and the header repeated per kind. With composition, Simulation and Calibrator take one type. A builder per kind (NetworkModelBuilder, …) The user writes the same transitions again for each kind. One structure per kind that holds its own transitions The same duplication, inside the model files. A setting of the engine that picks the structure A graph or a set of agents is data of the model, not a setting; the file would not reproduce a run. A structure that holds a reference to its process Two copies to keep equal: a model copied or changed would carry a stale process.

A structure may have variants: a subclass that keeps the kind, the fields and the engines of its structure, narrows the constructor and may add checks (MarkovChain(Aggregate), Network(Agents) in later proposals, #142 and #144). The JSON holds the kind and the variant; the Python registry (ModelStructure._kinds) is keyed by (kind, variant), so a model loads back as the class it was saved with. Rust reads the variant only to run its checks (AggregateVariant::check), so the engines do not change. A subclass with no tag would load back as its base class and compare unequal; a kind per narrower form would split the structures again.

The fractions of Aggregate are mappings by id (bin_fractions={"A": 0.99}), in Python and in the file, and Rust keeps their order (IndexMap). A list of {"bin", "fraction"} records needs a second shape for the constructor, and Pydantic calls a custom __init__ when it validates a file too.

Guards: crates/commol-core/src/types/model.rs (tests), tests/building/test_save_and_load.py, tests/model_kinds/test_interface.py::TestStructureInterface, tests/model_kinds/test_interface.py::TestVariants, tests/building/test_engine.py::TestBuild.

docs.title: Neutral terms carry a process across structures
docs.text:
A rate may read neighbors_<bin>, the amount of a bin among the neighbors of a unit, and neighbors, their total. They carry a process from one structure to another: a rate that reads them and no compartment is proportional, a rate per unit of its source, which a network or an agent model reads per node or per agent. Under Aggregate the structure says who the neighbors are, with no default:

Aggregate.neighbors neighbors_<bin> from a compartment of category g neighbors Complete() The bin total total Groups(stratification, weights) Σ_g' w[g][g'] × (amount of the bin in g') Σ_g' w[g][g'] × (amount of every bin in g')

plan_transition_flows (crates/commol-model/src/flows.rs) decides whether a rate is absolute before resolve_neighbors writes the terms as the sums they are, found by label (CompartmentLayout::with_category), so k1 * neighbors_B / neighbors from A is the proportional flow k1 × A × B / total under Complete(). check_model (crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs) reserves the names, rejects a neighbors_<id> that names no bin and a formula parameter that reads them, and asks for neighbors when a rate reads them; Neighbors::check checks the groups and their weights.

Every term is neutral: no "population", "size" or "contact", which assume individuals and a field. A default of Complete() would choose a modelling assumption for the user.

Guards: tests/transitions/test_neighbors.py, crates/commol-model/src/flows.rs (tests complete_neighbors_…, group_neighbors_…, a_rate_that_reads_the_neighbors_…), crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs (tests a_name_of_the_neighbors_…, a_rate_reads_the_neighbors_of_a_bin_only_when_the_structure_has_them).

docs.title: Compartments are labels with a name
docs.text:
A compartment is a bin plus one category for each stratification that applies to it, in declaration order. Its name, {bin}_{category}_{category}…, is for display only. Its identity is its label: OutputLabels in crates/commol-model/src/labels.rs and CompartmentLayout in crates/commol-model/src/layout.rs.

Rule: never parse a compartment name or match it by prefix. Bin A and bin A_x both produce names that start with A_, and a conditional stratification gives some compartments fewer suffixes than others. Use CompartmentLayout::find or of_bin in Rust, and the labels that the engine queries return in Python.

docs.title: State, amount, total and subgroup total
docs.text:
The library names what the compartments hold without assuming individuals:

Term Meaning Where State The vector of the amount of every compartment CompartmentalEngine::state, Engine.state Amount The value of one compartment InitialCompartment.amount Total The sum of every compartment, accumulators excluded; the initial fractions are taken of it InitialConditions.total, the rate variable total (SPECIAL_VAR_TOTAL) Subgroup total The sum of the compartments with some categories subgroup_total, the rate variables total_<cat>… (SUBGROUP_TOTAL_PREFIX)

The total is a real number, finite and greater than 0, so a model of a count, a mass or a concentration can be stated. 0 is rejected: every fraction of it is zero, and the report divides by it (initial_state in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs, InitialConditions.validate_total).

Rule: use these four terms in code, docs and tests. AxisPattern takes a value, so "amount" means only the value of a compartment.

Why, against the alternatives:

Alternative Why not "population", "head count", N They assume individuals and an epidemiological convention (N = S + I + R). A reserved N takes a letter that other fields use for a bin, such as a nutrient. "mass" A unit, not a quantity of any unit. "stock" An economic term, new to the code. "content" Ambiguous in software. "size" Reads as a count, and clashes with the NSGA-II population_size. A function total(g1, t1) No reserved names, but the expression language has no text arguments (jit/ast.rs), so the parser, the JIT and the security check would change.

Guards: builder.rs tests a_real_total_starts_with_amounts_that_sum_to_it and a_total_that_is_not_finite_and_positive_is_a_build_error; tests/building/test_reserved_names.py::test_a_bin_named_n_builds_and_runs; tests/initial_conditions/test_bin_fractions.py::TestTotal.

docs.title: Stratification order is part of the model
docs.text:
expand in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs applies the stratifications in declaration order. A stratification with conditions only expands the compartments whose earlier categories satisfy all of them, so the result can be a non-uniform product. A condition may only reference a stratification declared before it (ModelBuilder.add_stratification checks this).

Rule: changing the order of add_stratification calls changes which compartments exist and what they are named.

docs.title: Outputs are resolved by label
docs.text:
Aggregate.outputs_by_source(model) maps each bin or accumulator id to its output names in engine order. It uses the engine expansion (expanded_outputs), so Simulation.outputs_for, group_outputs and total_series group outputs by label, not by name.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_outputs.py::TestOutputsBySource::test_expansion_matches_the_engine_output_names (order) and TestSourceIdSharingAPrefix (a bin and an accumulator that share a prefix).

docs.title: The engine owns the variable names
docs.text:
The engine sets one variable per expanded compartment and per subgroup total (total_<categories>, bin totals and partial bin totals). check_model in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs rejects a parameter id that is one of those names, a parameter, bin or accumulator id that is an engine variable (ENGINE_VARIABLES: total, step, t, pi, e) or a name of the neighbors (neighbors, neighbors_…), a bin whose compartments or bin totals read as a total_<categories> name (two sums would share one slot), and a total_… variable in a rate or a formula parameter that names no subgroup total. Aggregate.check_model calls it at build, and CompiledModel::try_from_model calls it again. subgroup_total_names lists the names; Python reads them through the binding commol_rs.model.subgroup_total_names (engine_state.subgroup_total_names) to check rates and give units.

Rule: never list these names in Python. Ask the engine.

Guards: builder.rs tests parameter_id_cannot_be_a_compartment_or_a_subgroup_total, subgroup_total_out_of_declaration_order_is_a_build_error and subgroup_total_names_follow_the_declaration_order, an_engine_variable_is_not_a_parameter_bin_or_accumulator_id and a_bin_name_that_reads_as_a_subgroup_total_is_rejected; tests/building/test_reserved_names.py; tests/rates/test_expressions.py::TestSubgroupTotals::test_every_name_the_engine_provides_is_accepted_in_a_rate.

docs.title: Absolute and proportional rates
docs.text:
The flow planner (plan_transition_flows in crates/commol-model/src/flows.rs) decides for each flow whether the rate is absolute or proportional:

Case Rate is Flow per step A stratified rate sets absolute As set — The rate references a compartment, a bin total, total or a total_… variable Absolute rate The transition has no source Absolute rate Otherwise Proportional rate × source

A transition with several sources and a proportional rate is rejected, because it has no single source to multiply. Model.describe shows the planned flows, so a proportional rate prints as k1 * A.

The name says what the flow is: proportional to its source. The name "per-capita" counts heads, which assumes the source holds individuals; a source can hold a mass or a concentration. "Relative" would clash with the relative tolerance rtol of the ODE solver, and "per-unit" with units of measure.

Guard: tests/transitions/test_flows.py.

docs.title: The most specific stratified rate wins
docs.text: For each compartment, the stratified rate whose conditions match it with the largest number of conditions wins (helpers.rs). On a tie, the first one in the list wins. If none matches, the transition's default rate applies. Building a model fails if a stratified rate matches no compartment that the transition starts from.

docs.title: Formula parameters are evaluated every step, in order
docs.text: Parameters with a formula are evaluated again at each step, in the order they were declared (simulation.rs). A formula can use the value of an earlier formula from the same step. Declare parameters in dependency order.

docs.title: Compiled expressions are cached globally
docs.text:
JIT_CACHE in crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/mod.rs maps each preprocessed formula to one compiled function for the life of the process. The same formula always runs the same machine code, so results are reproducible.

Rule: do not invalidate or bypass the cache.

docs.title: Subgroup totals compose down the condition chain
docs.text:
The fractions of a conditional stratification are relative to the subgroup that its conditions select, not to the total. Subgroup totals therefore multiply along the chain: total × fraction(group1) × fraction(cat1). Aggregate.subgroup_total and Aggregate.get_conditioning_categories own this (context/aggregate.py); with per-compartment overrides, subgroup_total sums the state the engine builds.

Guard: tests/simulation/test_outputs.py::TestSubgroupTotal compares the result with the state the engine starts from.

docs.title: Calibrated initial conditions are applied in layers
docs.text:
InitialConditionPlan in crates/commol-model/src/initial_conditions.rs applies calibrated values in a fixed order: bins, category splits, exact compartments, and then the remainder named by CalibrationProblem.initial_condition_remainder. Both engines of the aggregate kind resolve and write initial conditions through it (SimulationEngine::plan_values and apply_values), and the calibration writes every value through the engine (ValueWriter in crates/commol-calibration/src/values.rs), so the objective, the predictions and the write-back (configured_engine, then the binding calibrated_initial_state) agree by construction. Aggregate.with_calibrated_values (context/_model/calibration_write_back.py) writes the values back as fractions, and pins as per-compartment overrides every compartment that the fractions cannot reproduce.

Guards: tests/calibration/test_write_back.py::TestApplyCalibrationParameters::test_applied_model_reproduces_the_loss_the_optimizer_scored; crates/commol-model/tests/initial_conditions.rs (the layers, the remainder and the targets of an id). See also Per-compartment initial conditions.

docs.title: Physical units are not in the model
docs.text:
A Model records no step length: rates are per step and positions and periods are step counts. The axis of a model is its independent variable, whatever quantity it is (time is one case), so the engines never ask which dimension it has. Model.step_unit is optional; only the unit check and AxisUnits read it. AxisUnits (context/axis_units.py) converts a value in any unit of the step dimension to steps on pint, and Model.axis_units() builds it from step_unit (or step) and the engine of the model. steps returns a float and snaps a result within 1e-9 of an integer to it; whether a position must be whole is the engine's check, not the converter's. The window grid is in api/windows.py.

The rate conversions (rate_from_mean_span, rate_from_probability) ask the engine: RateMeaning::rate_from_mean_span and rate_from_probability (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs) hold the formula of each meaning, so a new engine picks a meaning and Python does not change. The per-step rate from a mean span is 1 - e^(-1/n): it keeps the survival of the continuous process at every step, and its mean residence is 1/rate, not n (10.508 steps for n = 10). r = 1/n keeps the mean and loses the survival.

Rule: no formula of a rate per engine in Python; ask the engine.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_axis_units.py, crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs (tests a_rate_from_…), tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestWindowGrid.

docs.title: One step unit in the unit check
docs.text:
The engine converts no value between units. So UnitChecker._step_unit (context/_model/units.py) uses one step unit: the declared Model.step_unit, of any single dimension (check_step_unit), or else step, the default increment of any axis (dimension [step]). The check never infers the step unit from the parameters: a parameter in 1/meter may be a density, not a rate along the axis, and inferring only from units of time gives time a privilege that no other axis has. Without step_unit, a failed check says to declare it. The check reads the flows the engine plans (transition_flows, in UnitChecker._collect_unit_errors), so a proportional rate is checked as its flow, rate × source, and never by a rule of its own in Python. check_equation_units requires every flow to be equal to <bin unit>/<step unit>, and every impulse to <bin unit>, not only convertible to it (utils/equations.py, same_unit).

A unit means what pint defines; there is no list of aliases. A name that pint does not define becomes the one unit of its own dimension (define_units). In the check, t (a position) has the step unit and step (a count) is dimensionless. A number written in a rate and added to, subtracted from or compared with a quantity is read in its unit, as the engine reads it (parse_equation_unit); a computed number stays dimensionless.

Rule: never accept a convertible unit as equal. 1/week and 1/day in one model would read a weekly rate as a daily one.

Guards: tests/units/test_model_units.py::TestConsistentModels (test_a_proportional_rate_is_checked_as_its_flow), tests/units/test_model_units.py::TestStepUnit, tests/units/test_model_units.py::TestAxisUnit, tests/units/test_model_units.py::TestPositionOnTheAxis.

docs.title: Time inside a step
docs.text:
A differential model integrates in continuous time, but on [n, n + 1) its rates see step = n: t is continuous, step is the floor of t. A rate that reads step or a "pulse" series (and so AxisPattern.pulse, pulses, periodic) is therefore constant on its unit interval. When the right-hand side reads one of them (CompiledModel::depends_on_step), the engine ends a piece of integration at every integer, so each jump of the rate is the start of a piece (breakpoints in crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs).

A "step_function" or "linear" series reads t (SeriesParameter::evaluate), so it holds or interpolates from any position. The engine ends a piece at each of its points (CompiledModel::series_points), where the series jumps or bends. A difference engine reads t = step, so it gives the same values as before, and it rejects a point between integers.

A rate can also jump where t reaches a value it compares t with (t >= t_on, and so AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp). The compiler collects those values when they read only numbers, pi, e and parameters that do not change during a run (time_thresholds in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs), and the engine evaluates them with the current parameters and ends a piece there. Without that, an adaptive solver whose rate is 0 before a short window grows its step and steps over the window. A comparison with the state is a state event, which the engine does not detect.

On a piece [start, end) the right-hand side sees t no larger than the float just below end (RightHandSide::last_t). A Runge–Kutta step evaluates the right-hand side at the end of its interval; without the limit, a value that jumps at end would already act on the last step of the piece.

Whether an expression reads step comes from reads_variable, not from get_variables: get_variables leaves out the special variables, because it lists the variables a model must define.

Consequence: a proportional pulse p moves p of its source in a difference model and 1 − e^(−p) in a differential model. An impulse moves p in both. The alternative, step = t, makes a pulse step == n true on a set of zero length, so it would never act.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_differential.py::TestTimeInsideAStep, crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs::a_pulse_rate_is_a_constant_rate_on_its_unit_interval, a_rate_reads_the_step_of_its_unit_interval, a_rate_that_switches_on_t_acts_only_on_its_window, a_linear_series_matches_the_integral_of_its_interpolant, a_step_function_series_holds_from_a_position_between_steps, crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs::a_comparison_of_t_with_a_fixed_value_is_a_threshold, tests/axis_patterns/test_pattern_runs.py::TestDifferentialIntegration.

docs.title: Impulses come before the flows of their step
docs.text:
At step n the state jumps first, then the flows of the step run from the new state, in both engines (CompiledModel::apply_impulses). Every jump of one step is computed from the state before any of them. The output at n shows the state after the jump. With the other order, the differential output at n would show the state before the jump and the difference output the state after it, so the two engines would disagree at the output steps. A difference model needs integer impulse steps; a differential model stops its integration at each impulse step and restarts from the new state, so diffsol needs no event.

Guards: tests/transitions/test_impulses.py::TestJump, crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs::an_impulse_moves_its_fraction_at_once_in_both_engines.

docs.title: Windowed observations
docs.text:
An observation at at with window = W is compared with output(at) - output(at - W), anchored at its own position. The Rust loss and windowed_totals (api/windows.py) must give the same number, and the predictive reads windows through the observation operator (One observation operator). Window w covers (w · W, (w + 1) · W]; window_index places a position with max(ceil(at / W) − 1, 0), and observed_report calls it.

Guards: tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestAgreementWithTheCalibrationLoss (the loss at the generating parameters is zero), tests/reporting/test_simulation_report.py::test_observed_report_places_each_observation_by_window_index and tests/plotting/test_plotter.py::TestPredictiveSeries::test_a_windowed_band_of_one_draw_is_its_windowed_run.

docs.title: The engine owns positions
docs.text:
A position on the axis is an f64 in every engine call and a float in every public Python name (at); a length is window or period; a count of steps keeps num_steps. The SimulationEngine trait (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs) runs only at positions (run_at_positions_into_buffer); run(n) runs on the grid the engine builds, grid(n), and returns it. Each engine says which positions its model type accepts (check_position): a difference engine non-negative integers, a differential engine any finite, non-negative position. The engine checks every position where it receives it, and its message names the object that holds a rejected one: the observation or constraint (check_positions in crates/commol-calibration/src/calibration_problem.rs), the impulse transition or series parameter (DifferenceEquations::from_compiled).

Rule: Python passes positions on and shows the engine's message. It never checks whether a model type accepts a position.

Guards: crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_positions.rs, crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs::integer_positions_are_accepted_and_others_rejected, crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs::a_difference_engine_names_a_series_point_between_steps, tests/calibration/test_observations.py::TestPositionsAndTypology.

docs.title: Results carry their positions
docs.text:
Simulation.run and run_at return SimulationResults (api/results.py): a dict from output name to values, with the positions in positions and the rows in rows(). A dict keeps results["A"], json.dumps and pandas.DataFrame(results) working; a reserved key could clash with an output name. Windows, reports and plots read a value at a position (index_at, which matches within a relative 1e-9), never at a list index, so a model type that reports between integers fits them. A predictive holds the positions it was asked for (Predictive.positions).

Guards: tests/simulation/test_runs.py::TestResults, tests/reporting/test_simulation_report.py::TestNonIntegerPositions, tests/plotting/test_plotter.py::TestDifferentialModel.

docs.title: One list of engines
docs.text:
EngineType (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs) is the one list of model types. An entry is an engine, named by its type (DifferenceEquations, DifferentialEquations, StochasticEvents, StochasticSteps): a method, not a kind. It names the model kinds it runs (EngineType::kinds; today all four run aggregate). Each entry validates its settings and says the form of its dynamics (DynamicsForm: the schedule a description shows and the left-hand side of its equations) and the meaning of a rate (per_step or continuous). Engine::build (py-commol/src/engine.rs) builds the engine of an entry. A model holds its engine and the settings of that engine, Model.engine = {type, settings}, because the engine sets what a rate means, so a saved model reproduces its runs.

Python asks the list (commol_rs.engine.EngineType): it builds the engine, writes the left-hand side of an equation and the schedule of a description, and checks settings through it, and never branches on an engine name. It keeps the names of the engines only as the Literal EngineName (context/engine.py), for static typing and completion of ModelBuilder.build; a test checks that it equals the entries of the list (test_the_python_names_equal_the_engines_of_the_list). ModelEngine.type is a str that the list checks, so a model can name an engine of any kind; its settings are read with the class of that engine (ModelEngine.settings_of_the_engine), so a model loads back with the class it was saved with. Generating the Literal from Rust would need a code-generation step for four names; the test catches the same drift. An entry names the kinds it runs, so another kind (for example an agent network) adds kinds to an entry or new entries, not a second meaning of the type; see One interface for every model kind.

The builder takes the structure, the engine and its settings where it chooses them, build(structure, engine, settings=None), so one builder builds a model for each structure and engine with its own settings. Settings of one engine given to another raise an error from the engine that names both.

Guards: crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs (tests), py-commol/src/engine.rs::every_entry_builds_its_engine_and_runs, tests/building/test_engine.py.

docs.title: Every engine reads one set of flows
docs.text:
A compiled model is a set of flows (crates/commol-model/src/system.rs): CompiledModel::flow_rates gives the value of each flow, its rate times its source for a proportional rate (transition_rates gives the rate alone), and CompiledModel::flow_changes gives the change of the state of one event of each flow: −1 for each source piece, +1 for each target piece and each accumulator. Every engine reads them, and none has flow logic of its own:

Engine Reads DifferenceEquations derivatives, Σ changes × flow, added once per step DifferentialEquations derivatives, integrated StochasticEvents flow_rates as propensities, and one event of flow_changes at a time StochasticSteps transition_rates as per-step probabilities, and the drawn number of events of each flow

derivatives is flow_changesᵀ · flow_rates, computed piece by piece in the order of the old right-hand side, so the deterministic runs did not change by a bit. The deterministic engines are the mean-field limits of the stochastic ones, which gives the main test oracle. The positions where a rate can jump come from the same model (CompiledModel::breakpoints), so the differential and the continuous-time stochastic engines stop at the same positions.

Guards: crates/commol-model/tests/flows.rs, crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs::one_step_adds_the_derivatives_exactly, crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs (the_mean_of_many_runs_is_the_solution_of_the_ode, the_mean_of_many_chain_binomial_runs_is_the_difference_engine).

docs.title: A difference step never leaves an amount below zero
docs.text:
DifferenceEquations checks every compartment after the impulses of a step and after its flows (DifferenceEquations::step, settle in crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs). An amount below −10⁻¹² × total, the total at the start of the step, stops the run with SimulationError::Infeasible (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs). The message names the compartment, the step, its amount before the step and the flows that drain it (CompiledModel::outflows, impulse_outflows). The check reads the state and the right-hand side once, with no allocation, and the state stays as it was before the step. Accumulators are not checked: a net flow may count negative.

An error, for every cause, and not:

Alternative Why not A check only of proportional rates that sum above 1 None of the seven negative runs the test suite had broke that rule: they came from absolute rates on a bin total and from rates that turn negative. A warning A negative amount is never a correct state, and a warning inside a loop of calibrations is lost. Clamp the amount to zero The total is no longer kept, and the flows are no longer those of the model, without notice. Scale the outflows down to what the compartment holds A different model, chosen by the library; modelling choices belong to the user.

Calibration tells such a run from a failure by its type, not by its message. SimulationEngine returns SimulationError: Infeasible { position, message } for a state outside the values the model allows, and Failed(String) for every other error. The forward model turns an infeasible run into a Violation::InfeasibleRun and a failed one into EvaluationError::Failed (forward.rs); the optimization objective gives a violation a penalty and records nothing in the history; a failed run still stops the calibration, so a rate that cannot be evaluated does not hide behind a poor fit. An optimizer that explores the bounds of a rate would otherwise stop on the first infeasible point, though the fit lies elsewhere. A prediction of an infeasible draw raises InfeasibleStateError (prediction_error in py-commol/src/inference.rs). Python receives InfeasibleStateError, a ValueError (simulation_error in py-commol/src/engine.rs); a failed run stays a RuntimeError.

The differential engine is not checked: a solver may step below zero by its tolerance, and a model whose exact solution goes negative is a modelling choice there.

Guards: crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs (flows_that_move_more_than_a_compartment_holds_stop_the_first_step, a_rate_that_turns_negative_stops_the_step_where_an_amount_drops_below_zero, proportional_rates_that_sum_to_one_empty_a_compartment, an_impulse_that_moves_more_than_its_source_holds_stops_its_step, an_accumulator_may_count_a_negative_net_flow), crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_infeasible_runs.rs.

docs.title: Stochastic engines and seeds
docs.text:
A stochastic engine draws every random number from one generator seeded by SimulationEngine::set_seed (crates/commol-core/src/simulation_engine.rs); reset restores it, so a run is reproducible from its seed. The default set_seed does nothing, so the deterministic engines did not change. EngineType::is_stochastic says which engines draw: StochasticEvents and StochasticSteps (crates/commol-stochastic/). A run does not depend on the positions it reports at: StochasticEvents measures each wait from the last change of the state, never from a reported position, and draws the flow of an event only when the event happens.

Part Rule Generator Xoshiro256PlusPlus of rand_xoshiro, seeded by four SplitMix64 numbers of the seed (Generator in crates/commol-random/). Its sequence is the same on every platform and version. Samplers Exponential, Poisson, binomial and multinomial written in commol-random (sample.rs), not taken from rand_distr, whose values may change in a minor version. A test holds the first values of each for a fixed seed. Replicates Replicate i of seed s takes replicate_seed(s, i), the SplitMix64 of s + i. run_replicates runs them in parallel (rayon); a deterministic engine has no replicates. Calibration Common random numbers: the same replicate seeds at every evaluation, so the loss is a deterministic function of the parameters (CalibrationProblem::with_replicates). The user chooses the summary (ReplicateSummary); LossConfig computes it.

Reproducibility has three levels: the same machine and commol version give the same run; another platform gives the same random numbers, but the rate functions come from the system's libm through the JIT (math_expression/jit/libm.rs), which can differ in the last bit, so a run there is equal in distribution and rarely differs draw by draw; another commol version may change a run, and the changelog says so.

Alternative Why not A random source passed to every call The trait grows an argument that the deterministic engines ignore. The seed in the model file A model is a description; the seed belongs to a run, as CalibrationProblem.seed does. StdRng or SmallRng StdRng is slower and its security is not needed; SmallRng is documented as not portable. A pure-Rust libm in the JIT Costs speed in every engine for a difference in the last bit; the levels above are documented instead. One run per calibration evaluation The loss is noise, and Nelder-Mead stops anywhere. The mean as the default summary What to fit is a modelling choice; the mean of runs where half go extinct describes no run.

Guards: crates/commol-random/ (tests, with the stored first values of each sampler in tests/reference_values.txt), py-commol/src/engine.rs (a_stochastic_engine_repeats_a_run_from_its_seed, an_aggregate_stochastic_engine_repeats_a_run_from_its_seed, a_deterministic_engine_ignores_the_seed), crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs::a_run_depends_on_its_seed_and_not_on_where_it_reports, crates/commol-calibration/src/types.rs (replicate_tests), tests/model_kinds/test_stochastic.py.

docs.title: Whole units in a stochastic engine
docs.text:
A stochastic engine moves whole units, so it starts from whole amounts. check_model (crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs, called by build and by every engine) rejects a total that is not whole, and initial amounts that are not whole unless the settings of the engine name a Rounding (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs); the message lists both. There is no default:

rounding Start of each run (Units::begin in crates/commol-stochastic/src/units.rs) "largest_remainder" The same whole amounts: each amount rounded down, the units left over to the largest remainders, the first compartment first on a tie "random" A multinomial draw of the total with the fractions of the model, from the generator of the run

The engine rounds at the start of a run, not when it is built, so a value that calibration writes (InitialConditionPlan) goes through the same rounding, and "random" draws after the values are written. With no rounding, a written value that is not whole is an error.

Alternative Why not Largest remainder by default With small amounts the rounding is a modelling choice: half a unit in each of ten groups starts five groups with one unit and five with none, which decides which groups can start a process at all. The library would choose it without notice. Random rounding by default The same objection, the other way. Reject every amount that is not whole Most stratified models would fail, with no way out but to compute whole amounts by hand.

A per-step probability of StochasticSteps outside [0, 1], or proportional rates out of one compartment that sum to more than 1, are an error that names the compartment, the step and the flows (SimulationError::Infeasible), not a clamp: a binomial draw has no meaning outside [0, 1], and a clamp would change the model without notice.

Guards: crates/commol-stochastic/tests/oracles.rs (amounts_that_are_not_whole_need_a_rounding, the_largest_remainder_starts_every_run_from_the_same_whole_amounts, a_random_rounding_starts_on_average_from_the_amounts_of_the_model, calibrated_initial_conditions_go_through_the_rounding, a_negative_rate_or_probabilities_above_one_fail_at_their_step), tests/stochastic/test_whole_units.py.

docs.title: The solver is diffsol
docs.text:
The differential engine keeps no numerical method of its own: diffsol (pinned to a minor version, ~0.17.1) solves the system with tsit45 or bdf. bdf takes the Jacobian-vector product by finite differences (RightHandSide::jac_mul), one extra right-hand-side evaluation, because a symbolic derivative of every rate would be new numerical code. The matrix is dense (nalgebra) below SPARSE_THRESHOLD state components and sparse (faer) from there; diffsol finds the sparse pattern by passing NaN through J·v. Solver settings live in the model (Model.engine.settings), so a saved model reproduces a run.

Guards: crates/commol-differential/src/tests.rs (bdf_solves_a_stiff_model_within_the_tolerance, a_large_stiff_model_uses_the_sparse_path).

docs.title: One meaning of an observation weight
docs.text:
LossConfig::term and LossConfig::finish in crates/commol-calibration/src/types.rs compute every loss: sse is Σ w·r², rmse is √(Σ w·r² / Σ w), mae is Σ w·|r| / Σ w. The discrepancy (discrepancy.rs) calls them for the optimizer and for every method that reads the loss.

Rule: never write a loss formula elsewhere.

Guards: types.rs loss_tests; discrepancy::tests.

docs.title: Nelder-Mead searches inside the bounds
docs.text:
The objective clamps values to their bounds, so the loss is flat outside them, and a simplex that crosses a bound collapses there. Nelder-Mead therefore searches an unbounded u and scores x = lo + (hi − lo)·(sin u + 1)/2 (SineTransform and BoundedProblem in optimization.rs). Its evaluations and its result are recorded in x. converged is true only for SolverConverged and TargetCostReached (optimization::converged). An error of the model at a vertex of the initial simplex stops the run with its message (NelderMead::init of the argmin fork returns it).

Rule: report and record values in x, never in u. Every optimizer run, the verbose one included, goes through optimization::run.

Guards: optimization::tests; tests/calibration/test_optimizers.py.

docs.title: A Simulation follows its model
docs.text:
Simulation keeps the JSON its engine was built from. run, engine and simulation_outputs compare it with model_dump_json() and rebuild the engine when it differs (Simulation._sync_engine), and run resets the engine first. Calibrator takes simulation.engine when it is created, so the check is in the property, not only in run.

Guard: tests/simulation/test_runs.py.

docs.title: One observation operator
docs.text:
ObservationOperator (crates/commol-calibration/src/observation.rs) is the only code that turns a run into observed quantities: the row of each observation, the sum of its outputs, its increment over its window and its factor. The loss, the predictions of PyCalibrationProblem, the predictive's at_observations and every score read it, and the plotter reads a windowed or scaled series of a predictive through it. The calibration problem is split into one layer per job, each in its own module: ForwardModel (forward.rs) is the only code that clones, resets, writes values to or runs the engine; Feasibility (feasibility.rs) checks bounds and constraints; Discrepancy (discrepancy.rs) compares predictions with data; OptimizationObjective (objective.rs) is the argmin cost function. CalibrationProblem holds them, is built once and has no interior mutability; the buffers of an evaluation are a Workspace per thread.

Rule: Python never transforms a prediction of a calibration problem or of a sample: their windows, sums, factors, normalization, quantiles and scores come from Rust. Calibrator builds the Rust problem once (commol_rs.inference.CalibrationProblem) and every call reads it. The helpers that present results already computed, such as windowed_totals (api/windows.py) for a run or its replicates, are not predictions; they must agree with the operator, which tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestAgreementWithTheCalibrationLoss checks.

Guards: observation::tests, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_predictive.rs::observation_draws_are_the_predictions_the_loss_compares, tests/uncertainty/test_predictive.py::TestObservations.

docs.title: Constraints bound the support
docs.text:
A point is feasible, or it violates the problem by an amount: a bound, a constraint, an infeasible start or run, or a value that is not finite (Violation in feasibility.rs). Only OptimizationObjective turns a violation into a penalty, base × (1 + amount), where base scales with the largest observed value. An inference method sees the same violation as the edge of the support: its log density is −∞ (discrepancy_in_support in crates/commol-inference/src/target.rs).

Alternative Why not The penalty for every method Its scale is arbitrary, so a sampler would give weight to infeasible points. Reject and draw again, with no value A profile or a Laplace fit needs the value at the edge.

Guards: feasibility::tests, crates/commol-calibration/tests/test_infeasible_runs.rs.

docs.title: A sample carries its weights
docs.text:
A method with draws returns its own result type, which holds a ParameterSample (crates/commol-inference/src/sample.rs, py-commol/commol/context/inference/sample.py): names, bounds, values, log weights normalized to sum to 1, optional groups and the method that made it. Plots, reports, the predictive and the scores read the sample, never the result of one method. Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust; equal weights give the unweighted statistic.

Alternative Why not One generic result for every method Profiles, conformal intervals and jackknife estimates are not draws. A union of result types Every caller narrows it.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/src/sample.rs tests, tests/uncertainty/test_sample.py.

docs.title: Methods plug into one entry point
docs.text:
Calibrator.uncertainty(method: UncertaintyMethod[R]) -> R runs every uncertainty method, and Calibrator.identifiability(method: IdentifiabilityMethod[R]) -> R every identifiability method. Both kinds subclass InferenceMethod[R] (context/inference/method.py) and share one registry; each entry point refuses the other kind with a TypeError that names the right one. A method is three parts: a configuration that subclasses UncertaintyMethod with its result type (context/inference/), a runner in Rust bound in py-commol/src/inference.rs, and a result (context/inference/). It registers its runner in api/inference/registry.py; the entry point looks the runner up by the configuration's type and knows no method. A static type checker infers R from the configuration's type.

Alternative Why not One Calibrator method per technique A class with thirty methods that every method edits. Free functions Each repeats the simulation and problem arguments. method.run(calibrator) The configuration, in context/, would import api/.

Every random number of a method comes from the commol-random generator, seeded from CalibrationProblem.seed (replicate_seed). Coverage studies (tests/support/coverage.py, marker coverage_study) check that a method's intervals cover the truth at their level; they run weekly (.github/workflows/coverage.yaml).

Guards: tests/uncertainty/test_entry_point.py, tests/uncertainty/test_coverage.py.

docs.title: Sensitivities come from one port
docs.text:
Every reader of derivatives of the predicted observations asks SensitivitySource (crates/commol-inference/src/sensitivity/); only a source knows how its derivatives are made. FiniteDifferences is the first: central differences, one-sided of second order at a bound, with the step h = η^{1/3} · max(|θ|, w) (at most w / 8), where η is the output accuracy of the engine (SimulationEngine::output_accuracy: machine epsilon, or the rtol of the ODE engine) and w the width of the bounds. Each entry carries an estimated error, from the steps h and 2h and the accuracy of the runs; the structural rank counts a singular value only above the norm of that error (Weyl's inequality). The scaled sensitivities S_ij = J_ij · |θ_j| / s_i do not depend on units. A stochastic engine is refused: its runs change in jumps with the parameters.

Alternative Why not Each method differentiates on its own The step, the error and the scaling would differ between methods. Exact derivatives first Symbolic differentiation of expressions and sensitivity equations in two engines; a later source behind the same port. Machine epsilon as the accuracy of every engine With rtol = 1e-6 the solver's error over the step is a fifth of the derivative, and the rank reads noise. A fixed rank threshold such as 1e-10 Below the error of finite differences, so every model looks identifiable.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/tests/test_sensitivity.rs, crates/commol-inference/tests/test_identifiability.rs, tests/uncertainty/test_identifiability.py.

docs.title: Two verdicts per parameter
docs.text:
An IdentifiabilityReport gives each parameter a structural verdict (what any data of the design of the observations can determine) and a practical verdict (what these data determine). Only StructuralRank on the design of the observations gives the structural verdict; a dense design keeps its verdicts in its section. Merging reports keeps a verdict the reports agree on, and makes one they disagree on conflicting, with every reason. Thresholds and tolerances of the methods are required arguments: they are modelling judgments.

Alternative Why not One verdict A parameter structurally identifiable and poorly determined by the data, the usual case, would look like a conflict. Defaults for the thresholds A judgment hidden in the library.

Guards: tests/uncertainty/test_identifiability.py (TestReport).

docs.title: One confidence-interval convention
docs.text:
Every interval is a weighted quantile: the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution, interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights (statistics::quantiles in crates/commol-inference/src/statistics.rs). With equal weights it equals NumPy's method="hazen"; a weight of zero removes a value. ci_percentiles (api/inference/intervals.py) turns a confidence level into the two percentile points. member_statistics reduces each member to the quantity of interest first, and then takes weighted quantiles across members; taking quantiles first gives a band that describes no member. The replicates of a stochastic run (SimulationReplicates.quantiles), a sample and a predictive use the same quantile.

Alternative Why not NumPy's default (linear) with equal weights and another rule with weights Two conventions: a sample would change its interval when it gains weights. Harrell–Davis Smoother, but with no simple weighted form, and slower.

Rule: every new interval goes through weighted_quantiles or member_statistics.

Guards: crates/commol-inference/src/statistics.rs tests, tests/uncertainty/test_intervals.py.

docs.title: A description is data, rendered apart
docs.text:
Model.describe(layout) returns a ModelDescription (context/description.py): sections with a key, a title and blocks from a closed set of Pydantic models (Text, Table, Equations, StateGraph, Matrix). The sections every kind shares come from Model (context/_model/describe.py); a kind adds its own through ModelStructure.describe (Aggregate: context/_model/aggregate_description.py). The renderers (api/description.py) read only blocks, so a new kind renders in every format with no new renderer. The form of the dynamics and the schedule come from the engine's list (EngineType::dynamics_form), because one structure runs as equations or as events depending on its engine.

Part Rule Equations Computed by the code of the planner's flows (transition_flows), so a description shows what the engine simulates. The text rendering keeps the compact and expanded forms line by line. Diagrams Mermaid in the Markdown rendering, only for a graph that is not expanded; Graphviz DOT for every graph in a .dot file. Text, LaTeX and JSON draw none. Layouts "default": overview, entities, dynamics, schedule, initialization, parameters, outputs. "odd": the ODD protocol; an element commol cannot fill is marked TO_BE_WRITTEN. A section with no blocks is left out of every rendering. Alternative Why not A printer per kind and per format (the former print_equations) Every kind writes every format, and no caller can read or export the description. A free-form dict The renderers would guess its shape; typed blocks are checked by Pydantic and ty. An image (PNG, SVG) of a graph Needs Graphviz or a browser at run time, a dependency for a view. TikZ in the LaTeX rendering Needs node coordinates, so a layout algorithm; a PDF made from the DOT file does the same.

Guards: tests/description/ (test_equations*.py check the lines of the equations through equation_forms; test_rendering.py checks the snapshots of description/snapshots/, parses the DOT with pydot and compiles the LaTeX with latexmk when they are installed), tests/building/test_engine.py (every engine gives a form).

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
api/reporting.py returns blocks of data, not documents: simulation_report (observed values, series, accumulators) and applied_parameters_report (calibrated parameters, and the sections of the model kind: initial_conditions for an aggregate model).

  • A single run and an ensemble (replicates or a Predictive) differ only at the leaves (ReportLeaf); a predictive's members carry their weights.
  • The key order of each entry is part of the contract, because it changes saved JSON files.
  • Labels and summary figures belong to the caller, because they carry domain vocabulary.

Guard: tests/reporting/.

docs.title: Model files are written in full
docs.text: Model.to_json writes every field, nulls included. Dropping nulls is not round-trip safe: an uncalibrated Parameter.value or BinFraction.fraction would lose a required key and fail to reload. render_json (context/_model/serialization.py) keeps files readable by writing long numeric arrays on one line. It is internal on purpose: an output format in the public API becomes a compatibility promise.

docs.title: Public models forbid unknown fields
docs.text:
Every public Pydantic class sets model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid"). An unknown field, such as a misspelt or an old name (window_steps), raises a ValidationError that names it, instead of being dropped with no error.

Guard: tests/building/test_unknown_fields.py.

docs.title: Every user expression is validated
docs.text:
Rate expressions (context/dynamics.py) and calibration constraints (context/calibration.py) pass through validate_expression_security (utils/security.py) before they reach the engine. The limits are in SecurityConfig.

Rule: any new field that accepts an expression must call it.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Previous: Repository map | Next: Conventions

docs.title: Maintainer Playbook
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

Use this page before you make or review a change. It turns the Repository map and the Design decisions into checklists.

docs.title: Every change
docs.text:
1. Read the user-facing page of the feature in the User Guide.
  2. Find the owner in the Repository map.
  3. Read the tests next to that code before you change it.
  4. Make the change in the narrowest owner.
  5. Run both test suites (see AGENTS.md).
  6. Update the documentation as the mandatory definition of done requires.
  7. Run python .github/scripts/affected.py --closes <number> and update each open issue it lists whose current state, paths or assumptions the change alters: its body, and a comment that says what changed (Planning, step 4).

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• Do not duplicate an engine rule in Python. Add a binding instead, and call it from context/_model/engine_state.py.
  • Do not identify compartments by name. Use labels (see Compartments are labels).
  • Do not drop invalid input silently. Reject it with a message that names the transition, compartment or parameter.
  • Do not change saved formats by accident. Model JSON and report key order are part of the contract.
  • Do not trust a closed proposal as specification. A closed issue records past work; the code and this guide describe the present.

docs.title: Process (bins, stratifications, accumulators) and the aggregate structure
docs.text:
• [ ] Change the Rust type in crates/commol-core/src/types/ (process.rs, aggregate.rs) and the Pydantic model in py-commol/commol/context/ (process.py, aggregate.py) together. A check of the process by itself goes in Process; a check against the structure goes in Aggregate.check_model.
  • [ ] Update the PyO3 binding and _commol_rs.pyi if the type crosses the boundary.
  • [ ] Update expansion in builder.rs (expand) if compartments change.
  • [ ] Check that test_expansion_matches_the_engine_output_names still passes.
  • [ ] Update Building models and Model structure.

docs.title: Transitions and rates
docs.text:
• [ ] Plan the flows in flows.rs; reject what cannot be simulated.
  • [ ] Check the rate semantics.
  • [ ] Add a case to tests/transitions/test_flows.py, and check the dynamics section of Model.describe (tests/description/).
  • [ ] Update Building models.

docs.title: Expressions (functions, variables)
docs.text:
• [ ] Change crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/, including the JIT (jit/) and its tests.
  • [ ] Add a new function to SAFE_FUNCTIONS in utils/security.py.
  • [ ] Update Mathematical expressions.

docs.title: Initial conditions
docs.text:
• [ ] Change the Pydantic validation in context/initial_conditions.py and the engine rule in builder.rs (initial_state).
  • [ ] Check that Aggregate.initial_state(process) reports the new state.
  • [ ] If calibration can set it, update initial_conditions.rs in commol-model (InitialConditionPlan) and the write-back (context/_model/calibration_write_back.py).
  • [ ] Check that test_applied_model_reproduces_the_loss_the_optimizer_scored still passes.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
• [ ] Put the change in its layer of crates/commol-calibration/: running the engine in forward.rs, reading observations in observation.rs, bounds and constraints in feasibility.rs, the loss in discrepancy.rs, penalties only in objective.rs. Use only SimulationEngine: a rule of one model kind goes behind plan_values, apply_values or output_sums of its engines.
  • [ ] Convert new options once, in api/calibrator.py.
  • [ ] Check that tests/simulation/test_windows.py::TestAgreementWithTheCalibrationLoss still passes if the loss changes.
  • [ ] Update Calibration.

docs.title: Uncertainty method
docs.text:
A method is three parts, and plugs into Calibrator.uncertainty without changing it (Design decisions):

  • [ ] The algorithm in crates/commol-inference/. It runs the engine only through ForwardModel, reads observations only through ObservationOperator, sees a Violation as outside the support (discrepancy_in_support), and draws every random number from a commol_random::Generator seeded from the problem's seed.
  • [ ] The runner, bound in py-commol/src/inference.rs, and its stub in _commol_rs.pyi.
  • [ ] The configuration, a subclass of UncertaintyMethod[YourResult], and the result, in context/inference/; a result with draws holds a ParameterSample.
  • [ ] register(YourMethod, runner) in api/inference/registry.py (import it from commol.api.inference).
  • [ ] A coverage study (tests/support/coverage.py, marker coverage_study) that shows its intervals cover at their level.
  • [ ] A guide page under docs/guide/uncertainty/, a row in the table "Which method answers which question" of its index, and an API entry.

An identifiability method follows the same steps with IdentifiabilityMethod[IdentifiabilityReport] and Calibrator.identifiability; it reads derivatives only through SensitivitySource, adds its section to IdentifiabilityReport, and needs no coverage study.

docs.title: Model type (engine)
docs.text:
To add an engine to the list:

  • [ ] Add the entry to EngineType in crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs and to ALL. The compiler then names every match to complete in that file: its name, the model kinds it runs (kinds), whether it is stochastic (is_stochastic), its settings (EngineSettings, parsed and validated with deny_unknown_fields), the form of its dynamics (dynamics_form: the schedule a description shows and the left-hand side of its equations) and the meaning of a rate.
  • [ ] Write the engine in its own crate and implement SimulationEngine (for an engine of the aggregate kind, also CompartmentalEngine from commol-model); try_from_model rejects a model of another engine. A stochastic engine draws every random number from one commol_random::Generator, implements set_seed, and restores the generator in reset, so a run repeats from its seed.
  • [ ] Add a variant to Engine in py-commol/src/engine.rs: one arm in build per kind it runs (the pair of the engine and the kind), engine_type, dispatch!, plan_values and apply_values (and compartmental! for an engine of the aggregate kind). Add the crate to py-commol/Cargo.toml.
  • [ ] Add the name to the EngineName Literal in context/engine.py; if the engine has settings, add their Pydantic class to EngineSettings.
  • [ ] Run the tests of crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs, py-commol/src/engine.rs and tests/building/test_engine.py; they run every entry of the list.
  • [ ] Say what a rate means for it in the guides, and add it to Model structure and Running simulations.
  • [ ] Add the engine to Inside Rust: a box in the diagram and a row in the table.

docs.title: Model kind
docs.text:
To add a kind of model, such as an agent network (see One interface for every model kind):

  • [ ] Add the kind to ModelKind in crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs and to its ALL: its name and the types of value calibration may set (value_types).
  • [ ] Add the structure of the kind to crates/commol-core/src/types/ and a variant to ModelStructure (structure.rs). The compiler names every match to complete, such as Model::aggregate. The structure reads the process of the model; it does not hold bins or transitions.
  • [ ] Add its engines to the list, as in Model type (engine), or add the new kind to the kinds of an engine that runs it. Each engine implements SimulationEngine: plan_values and apply_values resolve and write the values of the kind, and state_outputs and output_sums name what an expression reads.
  • [ ] Add a variant to EngineValuePlan in py-commol/src/engine.rs.
  • [ ] Write a ModelStructure subclass in py-commol/commol/context/, with kind as a Literal default. Implement check_model and outputs_by_source; override series_label, uncalibrated_values, with_calibrated_values, report_sections, describe and check_unit_consistency when the kind has them. Reject in check_model a feature of the process the kind cannot run, and name the form that carries over. Import the module in context/__init__.py, so Model.from_json reads the kind.
  • [ ] Do not write a builder: ModelBuilder.build(structure, engine) builds every kind. Do not change Simulation, Calibrator, the reports or the plotter: if one of them needs something of the kind, add a method to ModelStructure with a default.
  • [ ] For a variant of a structure, subclass it with variant as a Literal default, and add the variant and its checks to Rust (AggregateVariant for Aggregate).
  • [ ] Give the description of the kind: override ModelStructure.describe with the sections it fills (entities, dynamics, initialization, design_concepts), built from the blocks of context/description.py; the renderers need no change.
  • [ ] Copy the tests of tests/model_kinds/ for the new kind, and run the Rust and Python suites.
  • [ ] Add the kind to Model structure, the Mental model and a guide page.
  • [ ] Update Architecture if the kind adds a crate or changes the path of a simulation or a calibration.

docs.title: PyO3 bindings
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep logic out of py-commol/src/: convert types and call the crate.
  • [ ] Update _commol_rs.pyi.
  • [ ] Rebuild with maturin develop --release --features test-kind before you run pytest: the tests need the test model kind.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
• [ ] Keep the key order of existing entries.
  • [ ] Put a section that only one model kind has in its ModelStructure.report_sections, not in api/reporting.py.
  • [ ] Use member_statistics (with the weights of a Predictive) for values across members, and ParameterSample.summary for parameters.
  • [ ] Update tests/reporting/.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• [ ] Let Dependabot propose the update; it groups updates monthly.
  • [ ] For a major update that needs code changes, open your own pull request and close the Dependabot one with a link to it.
  • [ ] The argmin dependency is a fork (MUNQU/argmin, branch development): change the fork first, then update Cargo.lock.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: • [ ] Follow Release process.

docs.title: Review checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The change lives in the owner that the Repository map names.
  • [ ] No engine rule is re-implemented in Python.
  • [ ] The change meets the documentation definition of done: the affected docs are updated, in the agreed format, and the doc checks pass.
  • [ ] Every new claim in the docs names a file, function or test.
  • [ ] The diagrams of Architecture still describe the code.
  • [ ] The tests that guard the touched design decisions still pass.
  • [ ] Each open issue that .github/scripts/affected.py lists is updated, or does not depend on what changed.

docs.title: Mental Model
docs.text:
Back to Codebase Guide

Commol builds compartment models from a declarative definition and runs them as difference equations, as ordinary differential equations, or as stochastic processes of whole units. Python owns the user-facing API and validation; Rust owns every rule about how a model becomes numbers. A model has a process written once (bins, stratifications, transitions), a structure that lays it out and sets its kind (today aggregate: amounts per compartment), and an engine that runs it; the generic layers work with any kind.

docs.title: What Commol is
docs.text: It is Evidence A Python library with a fluent builder of the process py-commol/commol/api/model_builder.py A validated, serializable model definition: a header, a process, a structure and an engine py-commol/commol/context/ (Pydantic): model.py, process.py, structure.py, aggregate.py Generic layers that work with any model kind Simulation, Calibrator, reports and plots use only ModelStructure; Rust calibration uses only SimulationEngine (see Design decisions) One model compiler for every engine: expansion, flows, rates, the change of one event of each flow, the right-hand side crates/commol-model/ A Rust difference-equations engine crates/commol-difference/ A Rust ODE engine on diffsol crates/commol-differential/ Two Rust stochastic engines of whole units: events in continuous time (direct method, tau-leaping) and the chain binomial crates/commol-stochastic/ Reproducible random numbers for stochastic engines: the generator, replicate seeds, samplers and a sum tree of rates crates/commol-random/ A JIT compiler for rate expressions crates/commol-core/src/math_expression/jit/ (Cranelift) A calibration problem in layers: the forward model, the observation operator, feasibility, the discrepancy and the optimization objective; optimizers from one or several starts crates/commol-calibration/, py-commol/commol/api/calibrator.py What every uncertainty method returns or reads: a weighted parameter sample, its predictive, scores, one entry point crates/commol-inference/, py-commol/commol/api/inference/, py-commol/commol/context/inference/

docs.title: What Commol is not
docs.text: It is not Boundary A domain library It knows bins, categories and rates, not diseases or drugs. Domain vocabulary belongs in user scripts. A numerical-methods library The differential engine delegates the integration to diffsol; Commol keeps no ODE method of its own (see Design decisions). A clock A model has no physical units: rates are per step and positions and periods are step counts, and the axis is the independent variable of the model, whatever quantity it is. AxisUnits converts at the edges (see Design decisions). A rule engine for transitions A transition has no condition. A rate expresses a gate, such as if(A > 0, k, 0) (see Mathematical expressions), and stratified rates set a rate per category.

docs.title: Model kind and engine
docs.text:
Term What it is Where Process What changes and how, written once for every kind: bins, accumulators, stratifications, transitions. Process (crates/commol-core/src/types/process.rs, context/process.py); Model.process Model kind How the process is laid out: the kind of its structure. aggregate: the bins expanded over the stratifications into compartments, each holding an amount. A variant is a narrower form of a structure with the same kind and engines. ModelKind (crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs); ModelStructure and its subclasses in Python Engine A method: how a model advances along the axis, and what a rate means: DifferenceEquations, DifferentialEquations, StochasticEvents, StochasticSteps. EngineType, the one list (engine.rs); Model.engine

Each engine runs some kinds (EngineType::kinds). A model whose engine does not run its kind is rejected when it is made, and the error lists the engines of its kind.

docs.title: How a model flows through the layers
docs.text:
ModelBuilder ... .build(Aggregate(...), engine)
                                   -> commol.context.Model[Aggregate]
                                      (Pydantic validation; the engine's list
                                      checks model.engine and its kind; the
                                      structure checks itself against the process)
Simulation(model)                  -> engine_state.build_engine(model JSON)
                                   -> commol_rs.core.Model.from_json(...)
                                   -> commol_rs.engine.Engine(...): the implementation of
                                      the engine model.engine.type names (EngineType list)
                                      for the kind of model.structure
                                   every engine of the aggregate kind compiles it with commol-model (CompiledModel):
                                        expand the bins of the process over its stratifications
                                        build the initial state
                                        plan the transition flows, resolve the neighbors, compile the rates
                                        flow_rates and flow_changes (one event of each flow)
                                        derivatives(step, t, X) = Σ changes × flows
Simulation.run(n) / run_at(at)     -> difference: X += derivatives, once per step
                                      differential: diffsol integrates derivatives
                                      stochastic events: one event (or a leap) at a time
                                      stochastic steps: a chain binomial draw per step
                                      (a stochastic engine: set_seed, then reset)
Simulation.replicates(n).run(…)    -> Engine.run_replicates: one seed per replicate,
                                      run in parallel (run_replicates, rayon)
Calibrator(simulation, problem)    -> commol_rs.calibration.calibrate(engine, ...):
                                      parameters by id; values of the kind, such as
                                      initial conditions, through the engine

The same model functions also answer questions about a process and its aggregate structure without a simulation: Aggregate.initial_state(process), Model.describe and the unit checker call initial_state, transition_flows and expanded_outputs of commol_rs.model through py-commol/commol/context/_model/engine_state.py.

docs.title: Invariants
docs.text:
These hold for every change. A pull request that breaks one needs a design discussion first.

  • Rust is the single source of truth. Python asks the engine how a model expands, which state it starts with, and which flows it has. It never keeps a second implementation of those rules.
  • Compartments are identified by labels, not by names. A compartment is a bin plus one category per applied stratification (OutputLabels, CompartmentLayout). Code never parses a compartment name or matches it by prefix: bin A and bin A_x must never be confused.
  • A model that cannot be simulated as written is rejected when it is built. The flow planner returns an error instead of dropping a transition.
  • Stratification declaration order is part of the model. Stratifications expand in declaration order, and a conditional stratification may only reference stratifications declared before it.
  • A run is reproducible from its model and its seed, on one platform and one commol version. The same formula always runs the same compiled code (global JIT cache); a stochastic engine draws every random number from one generator seeded by SimulationEngine::set_seed, which reset restores; calibrations accept a seed. See Stochastic engines and seeds.
  • What the user saves, the engine reloads. Model.to_json writes every field, and calibrated values written back to a model reproduce the state the optimizer scored.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Name the user-facing behavior first.
  • [ ] Find the layer that owns it in the Repository map.
  • [ ] If Python needs an engine rule, add or use a binding instead of re-implementing it.
  • [ ] Read the tests next to that code before you add new patterns.
