docs.title: Describing a Model
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

Model.describe() returns a description of a model as data: sections of tables, equations, state graphs and text. You can read it in Python, render it as text, Markdown, LaTeX or JSON, save it to a file, or draw its state graph. The description works for every kind of model, and it is built from what the engine simulates, so the equations it shows are the equations that run. Use this page to document a model, to check the equations Commol derived, or to write the methods section of a paper.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Described", bin_unit="item", step_unit="day")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="1/day")
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1, "C": 0.0}),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

description = model.describe()
print(description.render("text"))   # every section, in plain text
description.save("model.md")        # Markdown, with the state graph as a Mermaid diagram
description.save("model.tex")       # a LaTeX document
description.save("model.dot")       # every state graph, in Graphviz DOT

In a Jupyter notebook, model.describe() as the last line of a cell shows the Markdown rendering, with the state graph drawn (JupyterLab draws Mermaid from version 4.1).

docs.title: What a description holds
docs.text:
A ModelDescription has a title, a layout and a list of sections. Each section has a key, a title and blocks. Model.describe() builds the sections every kind shares from the model, and the structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (ModelStructure.describe):

Key Content For an Aggregate model overview Name, description, version, kind, engine, its settings and the step unit From Model entities What holds the state Bins, accumulators, stratifications and their categories, the expanded compartments dynamics How the state changes The state graphs, the compact and expanded forms of the equations, the impulses, the neighbors schedule How the engine advances, and the settings it advances with From the engine (EngineType.schedule) and Model.engine.settings initialization The state the model starts from Bin and stratification fractions, overrides, and the initial state the engine builds parameters Every parameter Value, unit, whether calibration sets it, description outputs What a run returns The outputs of each bin and accumulator

A section with no blocks is left out of every rendering.

dynamics = description.section("dynamics")
print([type(block).__name__ for block in dynamics.blocks])
# ['StateGraph', 'StateGraph', 'Equations', 'Text', 'Equations']

The blocks are a closed set (commol.context.description):

Block Holds Text A paragraph Table Columns and rows of cells Equations Groups of equations, each in plain text and in LaTeX StateGraph Nodes and edges; expanded marks the graph of the expanded compartments Matrix Labelled rows and columns of numbers, such as the weights of neighbors

docs.title: Formats
docs.text:
render(format) returns a string; save(path, format=None) writes it and, without format, takes the format from the suffix of the path.

Format Suffix Equations Diagrams "text" .txt Compact and expanded forms in plain text None "markdown" .md LaTeX math The state graph of the model as a Mermaid diagram "latex" .tex align* environments in a full document None "json" .json As data The graphs as data; ModelDescription.model_validate_json reads it back "dot" .dot None Every state graph, the expanded one included

The Markdown rendering does not draw the graph of the expanded compartments: a stratified model can have hundreds of edges, more than a Mermaid diagram draws. It gives the size of the graph instead. The DOT file holds every graph; dot -Tpdf model.dot -o model.pdf draws them with Graphviz.

The LaTeX document uses only standard packages (amsmath, amssymb, longtable, fontenc, geometry), so latexmk -pdf model.tex builds it.

docs.title: The equations
docs.text:
The dynamics section of an aggregate model holds the flows that the engine plans, after it has decided which rates are proportional (see Transitions):

Part Content Compact form Each transition and its flows, source -> target: rate. With units, each symbol shows its unit and each flow its resulting unit. Expanded form One equation per compartment. The left-hand side comes from the engine: [A(t+Dt) - A(t)] / Dt for DifferenceEquations, dA/dt for DifferentialEquations. Events For a stochastic engine, instead of the expanded form: one row per flow, with the change of the state of one event and its propensity (StochasticEvents) or its draw in a step (StochasticSteps). See Stochastic Simulation. Impulses Each impulse transition, the positions where it acts and the amounts it moves; an impulse is not part of the equations.

For the model above, the text rendering holds:

Bin Transitions:
t_ab (A -> B):
  A -> B: k1(1/day) * A(item) * B(item) / total(item) [item / day]

t_bc (B -> C):
  B -> C: k2(1/day) * B(item) [item / day]

Total System: 3 coupled equations (3 bins)

[A(t+Dt) - A(t)] / Dt = - (k1 * A * B / total)
[B(t+Dt) - B(t)] / Dt = (k1 * A * B / total) - (k2 * B)
[C(t+Dt) - C(t)] / Dt = (k2 * B)

Units appear only when every bin and every constant parameter has one; with some units missing, the equations show none. To check the units, use check_unit_consistency.

docs.title: The ODD layout
docs.text:
model.describe(layout="odd") follows the ODD protocol (Overview, Design concepts, Details), the standard description of individual-based and agent-based models, used for other simulation models too (Grimm et al. 2006, updated in 2010 and 2020). The same layout works for every kind of model, so a paper can describe an aggregate model and an agent model in one format.

odd = model.describe(layout="odd")
print([section.title for section in odd.sections])
# ['Purpose and patterns', 'Entities, state variables and scales',
#  'Process overview and scheduling', 'Design concepts', 'Initialization',
#  'Input data', 'Submodels']
odd.save("model_odd.tex")
Element What Commol fills for an Aggregate model Purpose and patterns Model.description; without one, the marker Entities, state variables and scales Bins, accumulators, stratifications, compartments; the step unit and how the engine advances Process overview and scheduling Each transition, where it moves, whether it is an impulse; the schedule of the engine and its settings Design concepts Interaction (when the structure has neighbors), stochasticity (from the engine) and observation (the outputs); the marker for the others Initialization The fractions, the overrides and the initial state Input data The series parameters, or "None" Submodels The state graphs and equations, the parameters and the outputs

An element Commol cannot fill says "To be written by the modeller.": write it in the saved file. The layout of a description changes which sections it has and their order; the format of render is independent of it.

References:

  • Grimm, V., et al. (2006). A standard protocol for describing individual-based and agent-based models. Ecological Modelling, 198, 115–126. doi:10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2006.04.023
  • Grimm, V., et al. (2010). The ODD protocol: A review and first update. Ecological Modelling, 221, 2760–2768. doi:10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2010.08.019
  • Grimm, V., et al. (2020). The ODD protocol for describing agent-based and other simulation models: A second update to improve clarity, replication, and structural realism. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 23(2), 7. doi:10.18564/jasss.4259

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] model.describe().render("text") shows the equations you expect.
  • [ ] Saved files use a suffix of the table above, or pass format=.
  • [ ] For a paper, layout="odd" and the markers it leaves are filled in.

docs.title: Example 1: Basic Three-State Model
docs.text:
A simple model with three states and two transitions:

from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Three-State Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="flow_AB", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="flow_BC", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

docs.title: Example 2: Four-State Model with Intermediate States
docs.text:
Adding an intermediate state between A and B:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Four-State Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="M", name="Intermediate")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.4, description="A to M rate")
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.2, description="M to B rate")
    .add_parameter(id="k3", value=0.1, description="B to C rate")
    .add_transition(id="flow_AM", source=["A"], target=["M"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="flow_MB", source=["M"], target=["B"], rate="k2")
    .add_transition(id="flow_BC", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k3")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.999, "M": 0.0, "B": 0.001, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

docs.title: Example 3: Periodic Rates
docs.text:
Modelling periodic variation in a transition rate:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Periodic Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k_mean", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k_amp", value=0.2)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(
        id="periodic_flow",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k_mean * (1 + k_amp * sin(2 * pi * step / 365)) * A * B / total"
    )
    .add_transition(id="flow_BC", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=365 * 3)

docs.title: Example 4: Stratified Model with Group-Specific Rates
docs.text:
Different rates per category group:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Stratified Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2", "g3"])
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.0003)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_g1", value=0.15)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_g2", value=0.12)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_g3", value=0.08)
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_AB",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1"
    )
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_BC",
        source=["B"],
        target=["C"],
        stratified_rates=[
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g1"}],
                "rate": "k2_g1"
            },
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}],
                "rate": "k2_g2"
            },
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g3"}],
                "rate": "k2_g3"
            },
        ]
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=10000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.25, "g2": 0.55, "g3": 0.2}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

print(f"B_g1: {results['B_g1'][-1]:.2f}")
print(f"B_g2: {results['B_g2'][-1]:.2f}")
print(f"B_g3: {results['B_g3'][-1]:.2f}")

docs.title: Example 5: Waning Effect (Cyclic Transition)
docs.text:
Entities in the final state gradually return to the initial state:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Cyclic Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_parameter(id="k3", value=0.01)  # Return rate
    .add_transition(id="flow_AB", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="flow_BC", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .add_transition(id="return_CA", source=["C"], target=["A"], rate="k3")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=1000)

docs.title: Example 6: Capacity-Constrained Rate
docs.text:
The flow from B slows as the downstream compartment C fills, and stops when C reaches capacity. The rate names B, so it is the flow itself; the factor max(0, 1 - C / capacity) never turns it negative:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Capacity Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_max", value=0.15)
    .add_parameter(id="capacity", value=100.0)
    .add_transition(id="flow_AB", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_BC",
        source=["B"],
        target=["C"],
        rate="k2_max * B * max(0, 1 - C / capacity)"
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.95, "B": 0.05, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

docs.title: Example 7: Multi-Stratified Model with Intersection Rates
docs.text:
A model with two stratifications and a rate specific to a particular intersection of categories. per_compartment=True makes A and B in the rate the compartments of each flow, so each compartment of A loses an amount computed from its own amount, not from the total of the bin:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Multi-Stratified Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(id="type", categories=["t1", "t2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k1_low", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k1_high", value=0.6)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_AB",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1_low * A * B / total",
        stratified_rates=[
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "type", "category": "t2"}],
                "rate": "k1_high * A * B / total"
            }
        ],
        per_compartment=True,
    )
    .add_transition(id="flow_BC", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={
                "group": {"g1": 0.6, "g2": 0.4},
                "type": {"t1": 0.8, "t2": 0.2},
            },
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

docs.title: Example 8: Subgroup-Normalized Rate
docs.text:
The engine computes the subgroup total total_<category>. This example divides a rate by the total of its subgroup instead of the total of the model. per_compartment=True makes each compartment of A lose an amount computed from its own amount, not from the total of the bin:

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Subgroup-Normalized Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.4)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_AB",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1 * A * B / total",
        stratified_rates=[
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g1"}],
                "rate": "k1 * A * B / total_g1"  # Divided by the subgroup total
            }
        ],
        per_compartment=True,
    )
    .add_transition(id="flow_BC", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

docs.title: Example 9: Conditional Stratification
docs.text:
A second stratification that only applies to a subset of the first. Here, the subtype stratification only expands g2 compartments — g1 compartments are not split further. per_compartment=True on flow_AB makes each compartment of A lose an amount computed from its own amount, not from the total of the bin.

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Conditional Stratification Model", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    # group applies to all compartments
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    # subtype only applies to g2 compartments
    .add_stratification(
        id="subtype",
        categories=["s1", "s2"],
        conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}]
    )
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_default", value=0.1)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_s1", value=0.15)
    .add_parameter(id="k2_s2", value=0.05)
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_AB",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1 * A * B / total",
        per_compartment=True,
    )
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_BC",
        source=["B"],
        target=["C"],
        rate="k2_default",
        stratified_rates=[
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "subtype", "category": "s1"}],
                "rate": "k2_s1"
            },
            {
                "conditions": [{"stratification": "subtype", "category": "s2"}],
                "rate": "k2_s2"
            },
        ]
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=10000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={
                "group": {"g1": 0.6, "g2": 0.4},
                "subtype": {"s1": 0.7, "s2": 0.3},
            },
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

# Generated compartments:
# A_g1, B_g1, C_g1          (group=g1, no subtype)
# A_g2_s1, B_g2_s1, C_g2_s1 (group=g2, subtype=s1)
# A_g2_s2, B_g2_s2, C_g2_s2 (group=g2, subtype=s2)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

print(f"B_g1:    {results['B_g1'][-1]:.2f}")
print(f"B_g2_s1: {results['B_g2_s1'][-1]:.2f}")
print(f"B_g2_s2: {results['B_g2_s2'][-1]:.2f}")

docs.title: Example 10: Parameter Calibration
docs.text:
Calibrate model parameters to match observed data:

from commol import (
    ModelBuilder,
    Simulation,
    Calibrator,
    CalibrationProblem,
    CalibrationParameter,
    ObservedDataPoint,
    ParticleSwarmConfig,
)

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Model for Calibration", version="1.0")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=None)   # To be calibrated
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=None)   # To be calibrated
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_AB",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1 * A * B / total"
    )
    .add_transition(
        id="flow_BC",
        source=["B"],
        target=["C"],
        rate="k2 * B"
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

observed_data = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=0,  output="B", value=10.0),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=10, output="B", value=45.2),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=20, output="B", value=78.5),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=30, output="B", value=62.3),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=40, output="B", value=38.1),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=50, output="B", value=18.7),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=60, output="B", value=8.2),
]

simulation = Simulation(model)

parameters = [
    CalibrationParameter(
        id="k1",
        parameter_type="parameter",
        min_bound=0.0,
        max_bound=1.0,
        initial_guess=0.3
    ),
    CalibrationParameter(
        id="k2",
        parameter_type="parameter",
        min_bound=0.0,
        max_bound=1.0,
        initial_guess=0.1
    ),
]

problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=observed_data,
    parameters=parameters,
    loss_function="sse",
    optimization_config=ParticleSwarmConfig(
        num_particles=30,
        max_iterations=500,
        verbose=True
    ),
)

calibrator = Calibrator(simulation, problem)
result = calibrator.run()

print(f"Converged: {result.converged}")
print(f"Iterations: {result.iterations}")
print(f"Final loss: {result.final_loss:.6f}")
print(f"k1: {result.best_parameters['k1']:.6f}")
print(f"k2: {result.best_parameters['k2']:.6f}")

model.update_parameters(result.best_parameters)
calibrated_sim = Simulation(model)
results = calibrated_sim.run(num_steps=100)

docs.title: Example: Axis-Pattern Driven Transition
docs.text:
A composed transition that changes along the axis: an opening pulse, a periodic event every 30 steps, and a continuous sinusoid baseline.

from commol import ModelBuilder, Simulation, AxisPattern

rate = AxisPattern.combine(
    AxisPattern.pulse(at=0, value=0.3),
    AxisPattern.periodic(period=30, value=0.05),
    AxisPattern.sinusoid(amplitude=0.005, period=365, baseline=0.01),
)

model = (
    ModelBuilder("AB-axis-pattern")
    .add_bin("A", "Source")
    .add_bin("B", "Sink")
    .add_transition("flow", ["A"], ["B"], rate=rate)
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=10000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
        ),
        "DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

results = Simulation(model).run(num_steps=365)

docs.title: Example: Sub-Group Specific Schedules
docs.text:
Different stratification sub-groups receive different patterns. The schedule is built by chaining AxisPattern.add_group(...) calls — the first call on the class itself, subsequent calls on the returned instance:

from commol import ModelBuilder, Simulation, AxisPattern

rate = (
    AxisPattern.add_group(
        conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "cat1"}],
        schedule=AxisPattern.periodic(period=7, value=0.05),
    )
    .add_group(
        conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "cat2"}],
        schedule=AxisPattern.periodic(period=30, value=0.05),
    )
)

model = (
    ModelBuilder("AB-stratified-schedule")
    .add_bin("A", "Source")
    .add_bin("B", "Sink")
    .add_stratification("group", ["cat1", "cat2"])
    .add_transition("flow", ["A"], ["B"], rate=rate)
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"cat1": 0.5, "cat2": 0.5}},
        ),
        "DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

results = Simulation(model).run(num_steps=60)

docs.title: Mathematical Expressions
docs.text:
Back to Home

Rates and formula parameters are written as expressions, such as "k1 * A * B / total". This page lists everything an expression can contain: operators, variables, functions, and the security limits. The engine compiles each expression to machine code (Cranelift) once, and reuses it at every step.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Expressions")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k1_periodic", value="k1 * (1 + 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * step / 365))")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1_periodic * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_ba", source=["B"], target=["A"], rate="if(step > 30, 0.05, 0)")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

results = Simulation(model).run(num_steps=60)
Where Example Evaluated Transition rate "k1 * A * B / total" For every flow, at every step Formula parameter value "k1 * 2" At every step, in declaration order, before the rates Stratified rate rate "k_g1 * A" Like a transition rate Calibration constraint expression "k1 - k2" See Model Calibration

Whether a rate is the flow itself or a rate per member of the source depends on the variables it names; see Absolute and proportional rates.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator Meaning Example Value +, - Addition, subtraction, negation "k1 - k2", "-k1" *, / Multiplication, division "k1 * B / total" % Remainder "step % 7" 0 to 6 ** or ^ Power "2 * 3 ** 4" 162 ( ) Grouping "(2 + 3) * 4" 20 >, <, >=, <=, ==, != Comparison, only inside if "if(step > 30, k1, 0)" ! Not, only inside if "if(!(step > 30), k1, 0)"

Precedence, from high to low: parentheses, power, multiplication, division and remainder, addition and subtraction. So "2 ** 3 * 4" is 32 and "2 + 3 * 4" is 14.

A comparison gives a boolean, not a number, so it cannot be multiplied: "k1 * (step > 30)" is rejected. Write "if(step > 30, k1, 0)". Rates do not accept && or ||; nest if calls instead:

in_window = "if(step >= 10, if(step <= 20, 0.05, 0), 0)"   # 0.05 for steps 10 to 20
outside = "if(step < 10, 0.05, if(step > 20, 0.05, 0))"    # 0.05 outside that window

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: Variable Value A parameter id The parameter's value at this step A bin id, without stratifications The bin's amount A compartment name, such as A_g1 That compartment's amount A bin id, with stratifications The total of all its compartments total The total: the sum of every compartment, accumulators excluded neighbors_<bin>, neighbors In a transition rate only: the amount of a bin among the neighbors of a unit, and their total. The structure says who they are; a rate that reads them and no compartment is proportional. See Neighbors t The current position on the axis. A difference model reads it at each step, so there it equals step; a differential model reads it anywhere step The step that holds the current position, floor(t): 0, 1, 2, … It is constant on each unit interval of a differential model; see Time inside a step pi, e π and e

docs.title: Subgroup totals
docs.text:
With stratifications, the engine also provides sums of compartments, the subgroup totals. Category suffixes must follow the order in which the stratifications were declared. commol_rs.model.subgroup_total_names (in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs) lists them for a structure.

Variable Sum of Example (group then type) total_<cat>… Every compartment with these categories total_g1, total_t1, total_g1_t1 <bin> Every compartment of the bin A <bin>_<cat>… The bin's compartments with these categories A_g1, A_t1; with every category, the compartment itself (A_g1_t1) 
from commol import ModelBuilder

def value_of(expression: str) -> float:
    """The value of an expression at step 0, read through a formula parameter."""
    model = (
        ModelBuilder(name="Variables")
        .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
        .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
        .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
        .add_stratification(id="type", categories=["t1", "t2"])
        .add_parameter(id="probe", value=expression)
        .add_transition(id="probe_flow", source=[], target=["B"], rate="probe")
        .build(
            Aggregate(
                total=1000,
                bin_fractions={"A": 0.6, "B": 0.4},
                stratification_fractions={
                    "group": {"g1": 0.25, "g2": 0.75},
                    "type": {"t1": 0.5, "t2": 0.5},
                },
            ),
            engine="DifferenceEquations",
        )
    )
    results = Simulation(model).run(num_steps=1)
    inflow = sum(series[1] - series[0] for series in results.values())
    return inflow / 4  # the probe flows into each of the 4 B compartments

print(value_of("total + 0"))        # 1000.0
print(value_of("total_g1 + 0"))     # 250.0  = 1000 x 0.25
print(value_of("total_g1_t1 + 0"))  # 125.0  = 1000 x 0.25 x 0.5
print(value_of("A + 0"))        # 600.0
print(value_of("A_g1 + 0"))     # 150.0  = 600 x 0.25
print(value_of("A_t1 + 0"))     # 300.0  = 600 x 0.5
Pitfall Result Suffixes out of declaration order, as in A_t1_g1 Error: the variable is not found total_… out of order, as in total_t1_g1 build fails and lists the valid total_… names A combination that a conditional stratification never creates build fails for total_…; <bin>_… is not found

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Group Functions Trigonometric sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2(y, x) Hyperbolic sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh Exponential and logarithm exp, log (natural), ln (natural), log10, log2 Power and root sqrt, cbrt, pow(x, y), hypot(x, y) Comparison min(a, b), max(a, b), abs Rounding floor, ceil, round (halves round up: round(2.5) is 3) Conditional if(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false)

For rates that change along the axis, AxisPattern builds tested expressions for pulses, windows, ramps and sinusoids.

docs.title: Common patterns
docs.text:
patterns = {
    "product of two amounts": "k1 * A * B",
    "frequency dependent": "k1 * A * B / total",
    "saturation": "k1 * B / (1 + B)",
    "linear growth along the axis": "0.1 + 0.001 * step",
    "exponential decay along the axis": "k1 * exp(-0.01 * step)",
    "cycle of 365 steps": "k1 * (1 + 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * step / 365))",
    "never negative": "max(0, k1 - 0.001 * step)",
    "capped above a threshold": "k1 * min(1, 100 / max(B, 1))",
    "only after step 30": "if(step > 30, k1, 0)",
    "safe division": "k1 * B / max(total, 1)",
}

To keep a rate readable, move part of it into a formula parameter: add_parameter(id="k1_periodic", value="k1 * (1 + 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * step / 365))") and then rate="k1_periodic * A * B / total".

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Every rate and constraint expression is checked before it reaches the engine (commol.utils.security.validate_expression_security). An expression that is not plain mathematics is rejected when the transition is added:

try:
    ModelBuilder(name="Unsafe").add_bin(id="A", name="State A").add_transition(
        id="t", source=["A"], target=[], rate="__import__('os')"
    )
except ValueError as error:
    print("rejected")
Limit (SecurityConfig) Value Expression length 10000 characters Nesting depth 10 levels Function calls 500 Variable name length 50 characters Numeric literal 1e12 Complexity score 1000

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Back to Model Calibration

Two functions turn a calibrated model and a run into plain dictionaries, ready for JSON: applied_parameters_report (what the model holds and what calibration set) and simulation_report (what a run produced, next to the observations). Both work for a single calibration and for a sample of the parameters, with the same layout. A third, identifiability_report, gives the verdicts of an IdentifiabilityReport as plain data (Identifiability).

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
import json

from commol import (
    Aggregate,
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    ModelBuilder,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    ObservedDataPoint,
    Simulation,
    applied_parameters_report,
    simulation_report,
    windowed_totals,
)

def model(k1: float | None):
    return (
        ModelBuilder(name="Reported")
        .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
        .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
        .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
        .add_parameter(id="k1", value=k1)
        .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
        .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
        .add_transition(
            id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total", accumulators=["cum_ab"]
        )
        .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
        .build(
            Aggregate(
                total=1000,
                bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0},
            ),
            engine="DifferenceEquations",
        )
    )

ends = [7, 14, 21, 28]
truth = Simulation(model(0.4)).run(num_steps=28)
observed_data = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=end, output="cum_ab", value=count, window=7)
    for end, count in zip(ends, windowed_totals(truth["cum_ab"], truth.positions, 7, ends))
]
problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=observed_data,
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k1", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.0, max_bound=1.0)
    ],
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=500),
)

calibrated = model(None)
result = Calibrator(Simulation(calibrated), problem).run()
calibrated.apply_calibration_parameters(result, problem)

applied = applied_parameters_report(calibrated, result, problem)
print(json.dumps(applied["parameters"]["k2"]))  # {"value": 0.1, "calibrated": false}

simulation = Simulation(calibrated)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=28)
run_report = simulation_report(
    simulation,
    results,
    at=ends,
    window=7,
    num_windows=4,
    observed_data=observed_data,
    accumulators=["cum_ab"],
)
print(sorted(run_report))  # ['accumulators', 'observed', 'series']

docs.title: applied_parameters_report
docs.text:
applied_parameters_report(model, result, problem=None, parameter_statistics=None, confidence_level=None) lists every number the calibrated model holds, and whether calibration set it. The parameters section is the same for every kind of model; the structure of the model adds the sections of its kind (ModelStructure.report_sections). An aggregate model adds initial_conditions:

{
  "parameters": {
    "k1": {"value": 0.4, "calibrated": true},
    "k2": {"value": 0.1, "calibrated": false}
  },
  "initial_conditions": {
    "total": {"group": "total", "fraction": 1.0, "value": 1000.0, "calibrated": false},
    "A": {"group": "total", "fraction": 0.99, "value": 990.0, "calibrated": false},
    "B": {"group": "total", "fraction": 0.01, "value": 10.0, "calibrated": false},
    "C": {"group": "total", "fraction": 0.0, "value": 0.0, "calibrated": false}
  }
}
Argument Meaning model The model after apply_calibration_parameters. result A CalibrationResult, or an {id: value} mapping such as one of sample.draws(). problem Optional. Adds the factor parameters, which the model does not hold. sample, confidence_level Optional. A ParameterSample: each entry gains its weighted statistics (ParameterSample.summary). A sample needs a confidence level. Entry Rule Parameters Only numeric parameters: formulas and series are inputs, not fitted values. total The declared total, with fraction 1.0. Initial-condition value The amount the engine builds, overrides included. Initial-condition fraction That amount over total, so every row shares one denominator. group "total", or the conditioning categories for a conditional stratification. An uncalibrated bin (None fraction) fraction and value are null. A sample Each entry gains an interval block (mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max, std, all weighted), and the report starts with confidence_level.

The key order of each entry is fixed (value, calibrated, then interval; group, fraction, value, calibrated, then interval), so saved JSON files stay comparable.

docs.title: simulation_report
docs.text:
simulation_report(simulation, results, at, window, num_windows, observed_data=(), accumulators=(), ensemble_runs=None, confidence_level=None) reports a run on one axis of windows. It reads each value at a position of the results (results.positions), so it works for any model type: a differential model reports at non-integer positions once the results hold them (Reporting at any position).

Block Content observed For each observation label: values, padded to num_windows, so it lines up with windowed index for index. An observation goes to the window that holds its position (window_index). weights, outputs and factor_id appear when a series uses them. series Each compartment output sampled at at accumulators For each accumulator: total (its final value), windowed (the gain in each window that ends within the results, as the loss compares it) and cumulative (sampled at at); each reading as a total and by_output Argument Meaning results SimulationResults of run or run_at. at The positions where series and cumulative readings are sampled; each must be a position of the results (ValueError otherwise). window, num_windows The window axis of observed and windowed. observed_data The observations to report next to the run. accumulators The accumulator ids to report. ensemble_runs, confidence_level The SimulationReplicates of a stochastic engine, one SimulationResults per member, or a Predictive, whose draws carry their weights. Every number becomes a {mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max} block, reduced member by member with the weights; the layout does not change.

The report holds only these blocks. Add your own envelope around them, such as a run label or summary figures in your domain's terms:

document = {"kind": "calibration", "at": ends, **run_report}
print(json.dumps(document)[:30])

docs.title: identifiability_report
docs.text: identifiability_report(report) takes the result of Calibrator.identifiability, or of IdentifiabilityReport.merge, and returns parameters (each parameter, in problem order, with its structural and practical verdicts, their reasons and combinations, or None) and sections (the evidence of each method that ran, by section name).

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The model passed to applied_parameters_report already has the calibrated values.
  • [ ] problem is passed when there are factor parameters.
  • [ ] at, window and num_windows match the observations, and the results hold every position the report reads.

docs.title: Running Simulations
docs.text:
Back to Home

Simulation runs a built Model in the Rust engine and returns its outputs: one series per compartment and per accumulator, with the positions on the axis they were read at. This page covers running a model, reading and aggregating its outputs, running it in continuous time as differential equations, and plotting them.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total", accumulators=["cum_ab"]
    )
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

simulation = Simulation(model)
results = simulation.run(num_steps=100)

print(simulation.simulation_outputs)  # ['A', 'B', 'C', 'cum_ab']
print(f"C at step 100: {results['C'][-1]:.0f}")

docs.title: Simulation
docs.text:
Member Returns What it does Simulation(model) — Builds the engine for the model. A model with uncalibrated parameters can be built, but not run. run(num_steps, *, seed=None) SimulationResults Runs from the initial state, with the model as it is now, and reports at the positions 0, 1, …, num_steps. Raises ValueError if a parameter is still None, and InfeasibleStateError if a difference step leaves an amount below zero (Amounts below zero). run_at(at, *, seed=None) SimulationResults Runs from the initial state and reports at the given sorted positions only. The engine decides which positions its model type accepts: a DifferentialEquations model any non-negative position, such as 0.5; a DifferenceEquations model only integer steps. Otherwise ValueError, with the engine's message. See Differential equations. replicates(n, *, seed=None) ReplicateRuns For a stochastic engine: an object whose run and run_at return SimulationReplicates, n runs with one seed each. See Randomness, seeds and replicates. is_stochastic bool Whether the engine draws random numbers. simulation_outputs list[str] The output names, in engine order: compartments first, then accumulators. outputs_for(id) list[str] The outputs of one bin or accumulator. group_outputs(ids) dict[str, list[str]] The outputs of several bins or accumulators, keyed by id. total_series(results, ids) list[float] The sum of all outputs of the given ids, at each position of the results. windowed_totals(results, ids, window, at=None) list[float] What the given accumulators gained in each window. engine engine The underlying Rust engine, for the model as it is now: the engine model.engine.type names (engine.engine_type). engine.step() advances it one step; engine.reset() returns it to the initial state.

Every run starts again from the initial state, so two calls with the same model give the same result (Simulation.run resets the engine first). To continue a run step by step, use the engine:

first = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
again = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
print(again["A"] == first["A"])  # True: it started again

simulation.engine.step()  # step 11, from where the last run stopped
print(simulation.engine.state[0] < first["A"][-1])  # True: A keeps falling

The engine follows the model. When the model changed after the Simulation was created, for example with update_parameters or apply_calibration_parameters, run and engine rebuild the engine from the model as it is now (Simulation._sync_engine compares model_dump_json() with the JSON the engine was built from):

model.update_parameters({"k1": 0.0})
frozen = simulation.run(num_steps=10)
print(frozen["A"][10] == frozen["A"][0])  # True: k1 = 0 stops A → B
model.update_parameters({"k1": 0.3})

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
run and run_at return SimulationResults (py-commol/commol/api/results.py): a dict from output name to one value per position, so results["A"], json.dumps(results) and pandas.DataFrame(results) work as for any mapping. The positions the values were read at are in results.positions.

Member Shape Use for results[name] [value at positions[0], …] Reading one output, plotting results.positions [0.0, 1.0, …, n] for run(n); the requested positions for run_at Reading a value at a position, windows, reports results.rows() [[every output at positions[0]], …], in simulation_outputs order Matrix operations, export

run(num_steps) holds num_steps + 1 positions: position 0 is the initial state.

rows = results.rows()

print(results.positions[:3])  # [0.0, 1.0, 2.0]
print(len(rows))              # 101
print(len(rows[0]))           # 4: A, B, C and cum_ab
print([round(value) for value in rows[0]])  # [900, 100, 0, 0]

docs.title: Randomness, seeds and replicates
docs.text:
A stochastic engine draws random numbers, so its runs depend on a seed; a deterministic engine, such as DifferenceEquations and DifferentialEquations, gives the same run for every seed (EngineType.is_stochastic in crates/commol-core/src/types/engine.rs).

Call Deterministic engine Stochastic engine run(n, seed=s), run_at(at, seed=s) Ignores the seed; results.seed is None One run from seed s; results.seed is s run(n) without a seed results.seed is None Draws a seed from the operating system and keeps it in results.seed, so the run can be repeated replicates(n, seed=s).run(…) Raises ValueError that names the engine: every replicate would be equal n runs, in parallel in the engine, each with its own seed 
print(simulation.is_stochastic)                # False: a difference engine
print(simulation.run(num_steps=5, seed=1).seed)  # None: the run depends on no seed
try:
    simulation.replicates(10)
except ValueError as error:
    print(error)  # The DifferenceEquations engine is deterministic: ...

Replicate i takes the seed derived from seed and i, the SplitMix64 of seed + i (replicate_seed in crates/commol-random/src/generator.rs), so a replicate gives the same run however many replicates run, and simulation.run(…, seed=replicates[i].seed) repeats it. SimulationReplicates (py-commol/commol/api/results.py) is a list of SimulationResults:

Member Returns replicates[i], len(replicates) One run, with its seed; the number of runs seed, seeds, positions The seed the replicate seeds derive from, the seed of each replicate, the positions mean() SimulationResults of the mean of every output at each position quantiles(levels) {level: SimulationResults}, at each position, by the one quantile (NumPy's method="hazen") member_statistics(output, confidence_level) mean, median, ci_lower, ci_upper, min, max of one output at each position, reduced replicate by replicate with the one quantile 
from commol.api.plotter import SimulationPlotter

stochastic = Simulation(
    ModelBuilder(name="Stochastic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .build(Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0}), engine="StochasticEvents")
)
replicates = stochastic.replicates(200, seed=42).run(num_steps=50)
mean = replicates.mean()
band = replicates.member_statistics("B", confidence_level=0.9)
SimulationPlotter(stochastic, replicates).plot_series()  # the mean and a 95 % band
print(replicates.seeds[:2] == [run.seed for run in replicates[:2]])  # True

The stochastic engines and what they draw are in Stochastic Simulation.

A run is reproducible from its model and its seed, on one platform and one commol version:

Where The same seed gives The same machine and commol version The same run Another platform, the same commol version The same random numbers (Xoshiro256PlusPlus and samplers written in commol, crates/commol-random/), but the rate functions (exp, sin, log, …) come from the system's math library, which can differ in the last bit between operating systems; a run there is equal in distribution and rarely differs draw by draw Another commol version A run that may change; the changelog says so

docs.title: Accumulators
docs.text:
An accumulator output starts at 0 and only grows: it is the total that its transitions have moved since step 0. Here cum_ab is everything that has moved from A to B, so A plus cum_ab stays at the initial A:

print(round(results["A"][-1] + results["cum_ab"][-1]))  # 900

docs.title: Stratified outputs
docs.text:
With stratifications, every bin and accumulator has one output per combination of categories, named {id}_{category}_{category}… in the order the stratifications were declared.

stratified = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Stratified")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(id="type", categories=["t1", "t2"])
    .add_accumulator(id="cum_ab", name="Total moved from A to B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k", accumulators=["cum_ab"])
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={
                "group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5},
                "type": {"t1": 0.5, "t2": 0.5},
            },
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

stratified_simulation = Simulation(stratified)
stratified_results = stratified_simulation.run(num_steps=50)

print(stratified_simulation.outputs_for("B"))
# ['B_g1_t1', 'B_g1_t2', 'B_g2_t1', 'B_g2_t2']
print(stratified_simulation.group_outputs(["A", "cum_ab"])["cum_ab"])
# ['cum_ab_g1_t1', 'cum_ab_g1_t2', 'cum_ab_g2_t1', 'cum_ab_g2_t2']

docs.title: Totals by bin
docs.text:
total_series sums every output of the ids you give, at each position:

total_b = stratified_simulation.total_series(stratified_results, ["B"])
total_ab = stratified_simulation.total_series(stratified_results, ["A", "B"])
print(round(total_ab[-1]))  # 1000: A and B hold the whole total

Do not select outputs by name prefix

[k for k in results if k.startswith("B_")] also matches an accumulator named B_events, and, with conditional stratifications, outputs may have fewer suffixes than their siblings. outputs_for, group_outputs and total_series use the model structure, so neither case can go wrong.

docs.title: Totals by category
docs.text:
To select compartments by category, use their labels from model.structure.initial_state(model.process): each entry has name, bin and categories.

in_g1 = [
    compartment.name
    for compartment in stratified.structure.initial_state(stratified.process)
    if compartment.categories.get("group") == "g1"
]
print(in_g1)  # ['A_g1_t1', 'A_g1_t2', 'B_g1_t1', 'B_g1_t2']

total_g1 = [
    sum(stratified_results[name][step] for name in in_g1)
    for step in range(len(stratified_results[in_g1[0]]))
]
print(round(total_g1[-1]))  # 500: g1 started with half of the total

docs.title: Windowed totals
docs.text:
windowed_totals turns a cumulative output into the amount it gained in each window of length window on the axis. Window w covers (w · window, (w + 1) · window], and each value is the output at the end of the window minus the output at its start. Both must be positions of the results.

per_week = stratified_simulation.windowed_totals(
    stratified_results, ["cum_ab"], window=7
)
print(len(per_week))  # 7: the complete windows of a 50-step run
Argument Meaning ids Accumulator ids; their outputs are summed first. window The window length on the axis. Must be positive. at The positions where windows close. By default, every complete window of the results (window_ends). Pass observation positions to get the values a calibration compares against.

The window grid and the same reduction work on any series with the module-level functions of py-commol/commol/api/windows.py:

Function Returns window_start(i, window), window_end(i, window) The positions that bound window i: i · window and (i + 1) · window window_index(at, window) The window that holds a position, max(ceil(at / window) − 1, 0); the inverse of window_end. Reports place observations with it. window_ends(window, end) Every complete window end up to end windowed_totals(series, positions, window, at=None) The gain of a series over each window 
from commol import window_end, window_ends, window_index, windowed_totals

print(window_ends(window=7, end=30))                       # [7, 14, 21, 28]
print(window_end(0, 7), window_index(7, 7), window_index(7.5, 7))  # 7 0 1
print(windowed_totals([0, 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28], range(8), 3))  # [6, 15]

A window need not be a whole number of steps: see Reporting at any position.

docs.title: Differential equations
docs.text:
A model built with engine="DifferentialEquations" runs in continuous time. The engine (crates/commol-differential/) integrates dX/dt = Σ flows(t, X) with the ODE solver diffsol. The flows are the same as in a difference model: the same transitions, rates, accumulators, outputs, calibration, reports and plots. Only the way the engine advances changes.

import math

from commol import OdeSolver

ode_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Decay")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.1)
    .add_accumulator(id="moved", name="Moved from A to B")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1", accumulators=["moved"])
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferentialEquations",
        settings=OdeSolver(method="tsit45", rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-8),
    )
)

ode = Simulation(ode_model)
at = ode.run_at([0, 0.5, 2.25])
print(round(at["A"][2], 3), round(1000 * math.exp(-0.1 * 2.25), 3))  # 798.516 798.516
print(round(ode.run(num_steps=10)["moved"][10], 1))  # 632.1: the integral of the flow

docs.title: Solver settings
docs.text:
OdeSolver holds the settings of the DifferentialEquations engine. They are part of the model (Model.engine.settings), so a saved model reproduces its runs. Pass them where you choose the engine, build(engine="DifferentialEquations", settings=...), so one builder can build the model for each engine with its own settings; without them the defaults apply. The DifferenceEquations engine takes no settings: the engine rejects settings of another engine with an error that names both (ValidationError).

Field Default Meaning method "tsit45" "tsit45": explicit Runge–Kutta 5(4), for non-stiff models. "bdf": backward differentiation formulas, for stiff models (rates of very different speeds). rtol 1e-6 Relative tolerance of each state component. atol 1e-6 Absolute tolerance of each state component, in the unit of the bins.

bdf builds its Jacobian from a finite-difference Jacobian-vector product. It uses a dense matrix below SPARSE_THRESHOLD state components and a sparse one from there (crates/commol-differential/src/solve.rs).

docs.title: Time inside a step
docs.text:
On [n, n + 1) a rate sees step = n and the position t, which moves continuously. A rate that reads step, a "pulse" series or a pulse pattern (AxisPattern.pulse, pulses, periodic) is constant on its unit interval, and the engine restarts the integration at each integer where such a rate can jump. A proportional pulse p on step n acts as the constant rate p for one unit: it moves 1 − e^(−p) of its source, not p as in a difference model. To move a fraction at once, use an impulse.

A "step_function" or "linear" series and the patterns AxisPattern.interval and linear_ramp read t, so they change at any position, and the engine restarts the integration at their points and bounds. In a difference model t equals step, so they give the same results as a rate that reads step.

A rate can also jump where t reaches a value that it compares t with, such as if(t >= t_on, k1, 0). The engine restarts the integration there too, so the solver cannot step over a short window. This works when the value reads only numbers, pi, e and parameters with a constant or calibrated value, and t is one side of the comparison: write t >= 10, not t - 10 >= 0. A jump that depends on the state, such as if(t >= A, ...), is not found.

A rate of a differential model is continuous, not a fraction per step; see What a rate means. Model.axis_units() gives the rate that the engine of a model reads from a mean span or a probability over a period; see Units of the axis.

from commol import AxisPattern

pulse_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Pulse")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="B")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate=AxisPattern.pulse(at=2, value=0.2))
)
all_in_a = Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0})
ode_pulse = Simulation(
    pulse_model.build(all_in_a, engine="DifferentialEquations")
).run(num_steps=3)
print(round(ode_pulse["A"][2] - ode_pulse["A"][3], 1))  # 181.3 = 1000 (1 − e^−0.2)

docs.title: Reporting at any position
docs.text:
run_at(at) reports at sorted positions on the axis, from the dense output of the solver. Observations (ObservedDataPoint.at), windows (ObservedDataPoint.window) and constraint positions (CalibrationConstraint.at) may lie between integers for a differential model: the calibration reads the engine at those positions (Observations). A difference model reports only at integer steps; the engine rejects any other position and names the object that holds it.

Windows, reports and plots read a value at a position of the results, so a window of 2.5 works once the results hold its ends:

ends = window_ends(window=2.5, end=10)    # [2.5, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0]
ode_windows = ode.run_at([0.0, *ends])
gained = ode.windowed_totals(ode_windows, ["moved"], window=2.5)
print([round(value, 1) for value in gained])  # [221.2, 172.3, 134.2, 104.5]

docs.title: Plotting
docs.text:
SimulationPlotter(simulation, results) draws one subplot per output with seaborn, and returns the matplotlib Figure. With the SimulationReplicates of a stochastic engine, plot_series draws their mean and a band of confidence_level (default 0.95), each replicate reduced to the plotted series first:

from commol import PlotConfig, SimulationPlotter

plotter = SimulationPlotter(simulation, results)  # the results of the first run
plotter.plot_series(output_file="series.png")
plotter.plot_cumulative(output_file="cumulative.png")

plotter.plot_series(
    output_file="custom.png",
    config=PlotConfig(figsize=(16, 10), dpi=150, style="whitegrid", palette="Set2", context="talk"),
    series=["B", "C"],
    x_label="Week",
    tick_every=10,
    position_label=lambda at: f"w{int(at) // 7}",
    linewidth=2.5,
    alpha=0.8,
)
Argument Default Meaning output_file None Where to save the figure. None only returns it. series None (every output) What to plot, one subplot each: an output name (B_g1) or a bin or accumulator id (B), which plots the sum of its outputs (Simulation.outputs_for). An exact output name wins. An unknown entry raises ValueError. observed_data None ObservedDataPoints to draw on the subplot of their label, at their positions (a differential model may observe between integers). An observation with a window draws the windowed line, which reads the results at every window end and start (ValueError when the results do not hold one). calibration_result None A CalibrationResult gives the factor values that scale the model. A Predictive draws the weighted median of its draws and their band of confidence_level, each draw read through the observation operator (sums, windows, factors). config PlotConfig() Figure size, dpi, layout and seaborn style. show_legend True plot_series only. x_label, tick_every, position_label "Step", every plotted position, the position plot_series only. Label the x axis, for example in weeks. The x axis shows results.positions. other keyword arguments — Passed to seaborn.lineplot, such as linewidth or alpha. PlotConfig field Default Values figsize (12, 8) Inches (width, height) dpi 100 Resolution layout None (automatic) (rows, columns) style None "darkgrid", "whitegrid", "dark", "white", "ticks" palette None A seaborn palette or matplotlib colormap, such as "Set2" context None "paper", "notebook", "talk", "poster"

To compare with observations:

from commol import ObservedDataPoint

observed = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=10, output="B", value=45.2),
    ObservedDataPoint(at=20, output="B", value=78.5),
]
plotter.plot_series(output_file="with_data.png", observed_data=observed)

docs.title: Stochastic Simulation
docs.text:
Back to Home

A stochastic engine runs the process of a model as whole units that move at random, with no change to the process: the rates of the model become the probabilities or the hazards of its events. Use it when the variability between runs, an extinction or the behaviour of small amounts matters. This page covers the two stochastic engines of an aggregate model, how a rate becomes an event, whole units, the methods and their cost, and calibration with replicates.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

builder = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Stochastic Model")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
)
structure = Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"A": 0.999, "B": 0.001, "C": 0.0})

model = builder.build(structure, engine="StochasticEvents")
simulation = Simulation(model)

one_run = simulation.run(num_steps=100, seed=1)
print(one_run["C"][-1] == int(one_run["C"][-1]))  # True: whole units

replicates = simulation.replicates(100, seed=2).run(num_steps=100)
print(len(replicates))  # 100 runs, one seed each
died_out = sum(run["C"][-1] < 10 for run in replicates)
print(died_out)  # about a third of the runs: the one unit of B leaves before it spreads

The same builder and structure build the deterministic model with engine="DifferentialEquations": only the engine changes.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text: You need Engine The mean behaviour of a large amount DifferentialEquations or DifferenceEquations How much runs vary, and the spread of an output StochasticEvents or StochasticSteps The chance that an amount reaches zero and stays there (extinction) StochasticEvents or StochasticSteps Small amounts, where a unit more or less changes the outcome StochasticEvents or StochasticSteps

docs.title: The two engines
docs.text:
Engine Time Method Rate meaning Positions Crate StochasticEvents Continuous Gillespie's direct method (the stochastic simulation algorithm, SSA), or tau-leaping continuous: a hazard per unit of the axis Any finite, non-negative position commol-stochastic StochasticSteps Discrete steps The chain binomial per_step: a probability per step Integer steps commol-stochastic

Their mean-field limits are the deterministic engines: the expected change of the state of StochasticEvents is the right-hand side of DifferentialEquations, and the expected step of StochasticSteps is the step of DifferenceEquations while no cap acts (see below). A rate keeps its meaning: a per_step rate of a difference model is the probability of the chain binomial, and a continuous rate of a differential model is the hazard of the events (What a rate means).

docs.title: How a rate becomes an event
docs.text:
Each flow of the model is one kind of event. An event moves one unit: it takes one from each source of the flow, and adds one to each target and to each accumulator that counts the flow (CompiledModel::flow_changes in crates/commol-model/src/system.rs).

Rate StochasticEvents (propensity) StochasticSteps (draw of a step) Proportional, k Each unit of the source leaves at hazard k: propensity k × source Each unit leaves with probability k: Binomial(source, k) Absolute, r Events at rate r Poisson(r), capped by what the sources still hold No source (inflow), r Events at rate r Poisson(r)
  • StochasticEvents: a flow has no events while a source holds fewer units than an event takes. A negative propensity is an error that names the flow.
  • StochasticSteps: every draw reads the state at the start of the step. The units of one compartment leave by its proportional flows in one multinomial draw (each flow with its probability, staying with 1 − Σ k), so a unit never leaves twice and an amount never goes below zero. The absolute flows then draw in the order of the model, each capped by what its sources still hold. A negative rate, a proportional rate above 1, or proportional rates out of one compartment that sum to more than 1 raise InfeasibleStateError, which names the compartment, the step and the flows (StochasticSteps::step in crates/commol-stochastic/src/steps.rs).
from commol import InfeasibleStateError

too_likely = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Too likely")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.7)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.5)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1")
    .add_transition(id="t_ac", source=["A"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(structure, engine="StochasticSteps")
)
try:
    Simulation(too_likely).run(num_steps=5, seed=1)
except InfeasibleStateError as error:
    print(error)  # At step 0, the proportional rates out of compartment 'A': flows 't_ab' 0.7, 't_ac' 0.5 sum to 1.2, above 1. ...

Model.describe() shows the events in its dynamics section: one row per flow with its change of the state and its propensity or its draw (Describing a Model):

print(model.describe().render("markdown").split("### Events")[1].split("\n\n")[1])
# | Transition | Change | Propensity |
# |---|---|---|
# | t_ab | A -1, B +1 | k1 * A * B / total |
# | t_bc | B -1, C +1 | k2 * B |

docs.title: Whole units
docs.text:
A stochastic engine moves whole units, so it starts from whole amounts (check_model in crates/commol-model/src/builder.rs):

Initial amounts What happens The total is not a whole number build raises ValueError and names the engine Every amount is whole Nothing more is needed An amount is not whole build raises ValueError, unless the settings of the engine name a rounding; the message lists both

There is no default rounding: with small amounts the rounding decides which compartments start with a unit, so it is a modelling choice. Half a unit in each of ten groups starts five groups with one unit and five with none.

rounding Start of each run "largest_remainder" The same whole amounts in every run: each amount rounded down, and the units left over to the largest remainders, so they sum to the total "random" A multinomial draw of the total with the fractions of the model, in each run, so the mean start equals the amounts of the model 
from commol import StochasticEventsSettings

groups = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Groups")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=[f"g{i}" for i in range(10)])
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * B / total")
)
seeded = Aggregate(
    total=1000,
    bin_fractions={"A": 0.995, "B": 0.005},
    stratification_fractions={"group": {f"g{i}": 0.1 for i in range(10)}},
)
try:
    groups.build(seeded, engine="StochasticEvents")
except ValueError as error:
    print("largest_remainder" in str(error), "random" in str(error))  # True True

grouped = groups.build(
    seeded,
    engine="StochasticEvents",
    settings=StochasticEventsSettings(rounding="random"),
)
start = Simulation(grouped).run_at([0.0], seed=3)
print(sum(start[f"B_g{i}"][0] for i in range(10)) + sum(start[f"A_g{i}"][0] for i in range(10)))
# 1000.0

Initial conditions that calibration sets go through the same rounding. With no rounding, a calibrated value that is not whole is an error that lists the two options.

docs.title: Seeds and replicates
docs.text:
A run is reproducible from its model and its seed: simulation.run(…, seed=s) gives one run, and simulation.replicates(n, seed=s).run(…) gives n runs with one seed each, in parallel. A run does not depend on the positions it reports at: the output at a position is the state after the last event before it. See Randomness, seeds and replicates for the seeds, SimulationReplicates and its statistics, plots of the mean and a band, and reports.

again = simulation.run(num_steps=100, seed=1)
print(again == one_run)  # True
print(replicates.member_statistics("C", confidence_level=0.9)["ci_lower"][-1] >= 0)  # True

docs.title: Methods and their cost
docs.text:
StochasticEvents takes StochasticEventsSettings, and StochasticSteps takes StochasticStepsSettings (only rounding):

Setting Default Meaning method "direct" "direct": one event at a time, exact. "tau_leaping": a Poisson number of events of each flow in a leap, an approximation tau None The length of a leap of "tau_leaping"; None chooses each leap as Cao, Gillespie and Petzold (2006) do epsilon 0.03 How much a propensity may change in a chosen leap, relative to its value tolerance 1e-8 Relative tolerance of the time of an event when a rate reads t rounding None See Whole units
  • Cost of the direct method. The number of events grows with the total and with the rates: every unit that moves is one event. For a large total, use "tau_leaping" or a deterministic engine.
  • Tau-leaping. A chosen leap is as long as the propensities allow while they change by less than epsilon; a leap that would hold fewer than ten events is one exact event instead, and a leap that leaves an amount below zero is halved and drawn again. A fixed tau is first-order accurate: a smaller tau is closer to the direct method.
  • Rates that read t. Between events the state is fixed, but a rate that reads t, such as k * (1 + sin(t)), still changes. The direct method then integrates the total propensity from the last event until it reaches an exponential draw (a time change, Anderson 2007), within tolerance. A model whose rates do not read t pays nothing for it.
  • Breakpoints. The engine stops at every position where a rate can jump (the impulses, the values a rate compares t with, the points of a series read at t, and every integer when a rate reads step), so no wait and no leap crosses one (CompiledModel::breakpoints).
  • Impulses. At its positions, before the events there, a proportional impulse moves a binomial draw of its source (its rate is the probability that one unit moves, between 0 and 1); an absolute impulse moves its rate, a whole number of units. Each moves at most what its sources still hold.
leaping = builder.build(
    structure,
    engine="StochasticEvents",
    settings=StochasticEventsSettings(method="tau_leaping"),
)
leaped = Simulation(leaping).replicates(100, seed=2).run(num_steps=100)
print(abs(leaped.mean()["C"][-1] - replicates.mean()["C"][-1]) < 150)  # True

docs.title: Calibration with replicates
docs.text:
A calibration of a stochastic model runs replicates runs per evaluation with common random numbers, and compares the observations with the summary of the replicates you choose: "mean", "median", Quantile(q) or "crps" (Stochastic engines).

from commol import (
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    ObservedDataPoint,
)

mean = replicates.mean()
observed = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=at, output="C", value=mean["C"][at]) for at in (40, 70, 100)
]
unknown = builder.build(structure, engine="StochasticEvents")
unknown.update_parameters({"k2": None})
problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=observed,
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k2", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.01, max_bound=0.5)
    ],
    loss_function="sse",
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=100),
    replicates=50,
    replicate_summary="mean",
    seed=7,
)
result = Calibrator(Simulation(unknown), problem).run()
print(0.05 < result.best_parameters["k2"] < 0.2)  # True: near 0.1

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] The engine is StochasticEvents (continuous time) or StochasticSteps (per-step probabilities), as the rates of the model mean.
  • [ ] The total is whole, and the settings name a rounding when an amount is not.
  • [ ] Every run has a seed, or keeps the one commol drew (results.seed).
  • [ ] A large total uses "tau_leaping" or a deterministic engine.
  • [ ] A calibration sets replicates, replicate_summary and seed.
