docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

A transition moves an amount at every step: from its source compartments to its target compartments, at the rate you give. This page documents ModelBuilder.add_transition completely: rates, several sources, transitions between categories, stratified rates, impulses, amounts below zero, and what build checks.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder, Simulation

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Transitions")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

print(model.describe().render("text"))  # every flow, as the engine computes it

docs.title: add_transition
docs.text: Argument Type Default Meaning id str required The identifier. source list[str] required Bins (or one category) that lose the flow. [] means the flow enters the system. target list[str] required Bins (or one category) that gain the flow. [] means the flow leaves the system. rate str, float, AxisPattern or None None The rate formula; see Rates. With stratified_rates, the fallback rate. None with no stratified rate gives a transition with no flows. stratified_rates list[dict] \| None None Rates for some categories; see Stratified rates. per_compartment bool \| None None Replaces bin names in the rate with each flow's own compartment; see per_compartment. accumulators list[str] \| None None Accumulators that count the flow; see Building Models. impulse_at list[float] \| None None Makes the transition an impulse at these steps; see Impulses. impulse_every tuple[float, float] \| None None (period, offset): an impulse at offset, offset + period, …; see Impulses.

docs.title: Rates
docs.text: A rate is a formula (a string), a number, or a AxisPattern. A formula can use parameters, compartments, bin totals, total, step, constants and functions; see Mathematical Expressions.

docs.title: Absolute and proportional rates
docs.text:
The engine decides for each flow whether its rate is the flow itself or a rate per member of the source:

Case Kind Flow The rate names a compartment, a bin total, total or a total_… variable Absolute rate The transition has no source Absolute rate A stratified rate sets "absolute": True or False As set — Otherwise Proportional rate × source Rate Kind Flow from B to C "k2" Proportional k2 * B "k2 * B" Absolute k2 * B "k1 * A * B / total" Absolute k1 * A * B / total "0.5" with source=[] Absolute 0.5 enters the target

The description of the model shows every flow after this decision, so a proportional rate appears multiplied by its source.

docs.title: Rates that change along the axis
docs.text:
A formula may use step (or t), the current step:

periodic = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Periodic")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.3)
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k1 * (1 + 0.3 * sin(2 * pi * step / 365)) * A * B / total",
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

For pulses, windows, ramps and schedules per group, use Axis Patterns.

docs.title: Several sources or targets
docs.text:
A transition with several sources or targets moves one flow: every entry in source loses it and every entry in target gains it. A bin listed twice loses or gains it twice. The rate must be absolute.

merge = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Merge")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.001)
    .add_transition(id="t1", source=["A", "B"], target=["C", "C"], rate="k * A * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.5, "B": 0.5, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(merge.describe().render("text"))
# A loses k * A * B, B loses k * A * B, C gains 2 * (k * A * B)

docs.title: The $compartment placeholder
docs.text:
For independent flows with one formula, write $compartment in the rate. The builder creates one transition per source (or per target), named {id}__{compartment}, with $compartment replaced by that compartment:

outflow = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Outflow")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="mu", value=0.01)
    .add_transition(
        id="outflow",
        source=["A", "B", "C"],
        target=[],
        rate="mu * $compartment * (1 + 0.1 * $compartment / total)",
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.4, "B": 0.3, "C": 0.3},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

for transition in outflow.process.transitions:
    print(transition.id, transition.rate)
# outflow__A mu * A * (1 + 0.1 * A / total)
# outflow__B mu * B * (1 + 0.1 * B / total)
# outflow__C mu * C * (1 + 0.1 * C / total)
Rule Otherwise Several sources with one or no target, or several targets with one or no source ValueError: the mapping would be ambiguous At least two sources or two targets ValueError: write the compartment name instead A rate is given ValueError

stratified_rates may also use $compartment; each generated transition gets its own copy.

docs.title: Transitions between categories
docs.text:
When source and target are categories of one stratification, the transition moves amounts between them in every bin:

moving = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Moving")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="move", source=["g1"], target=["g2"], rate="k")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.5, "B": 0.5},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(moving.describe().render("text"))
# move (g1 -> g2):  A_g1 -> A_g2: k * A_g1   and   B_g1 -> B_g2: k * B_g1

A category transition needs exactly one source and one target category. If the target category is split by a conditional stratification, every flow must say which of its categories it enters, with a to condition (see Redirecting the target with to); otherwise build raises.

docs.title: per_compartment
docs.text:
With stratifications, a bin id in a rate means the total of the bin. In a flow from A_g1, "k * A" uses A_g1 + A_g2. per_compartment=True replaces each source and target bin id with the flow's own compartment:

Flow rate="k * A" with per_compartment=True A_g1 -> B_g1 k * A (the total) k * A_g1 A_g2 -> B_g2 k * A (the total) k * A_g2 
own_compartment = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Per compartment")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="t", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k * A", per_compartment=True)
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.5, "B": 0.5},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(own_compartment.describe().render("text"))
# A_g1 -> B_g1: k * A_g1   and   A_g2 -> B_g2: k * A_g2

It applies to the fallback rate and to every stratified rate, and only to transitions between bins.

docs.title: Stratified rates
docs.text:
stratified_rates gives some categories their own rate. Each entry has conditions and a rate, and may set absolute:

group_rates = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Group rates")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2", "g3"])
    .add_parameter(id="k_g1", value=0.15)
    .add_parameter(id="k_g2", value=0.10)
    .add_parameter(id="k_default", value=0.05)
    .add_transition(
        id="t_ab",
        source=["A"],
        target=["B"],
        rate="k_default",
        stratified_rates=[
            {"conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g1"}], "rate": "k_g1"},
            {"conditions": [{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}], "rate": "k_g2"},
        ],
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=900,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
            stratification_fractions={"group": {"g1": 0.3, "g2": 0.3, "g3": 0.4}},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(group_rates.describe().render("text"))
# A_g1 -> B_g1: k_g1 * A_g1,  A_g2 -> B_g2: k_g2 * A_g2,  A_g3 -> B_g3: k_default * A_g3
Entry key Type Meaning conditions list[dict] All must match the source compartment (AND). rate str or float The rate for matching compartments. absolute bool, optional Forces the rate to be absolute or proportional. Condition key Meaning stratification The stratification id. category Optional. The category the source must have. to Optional. The category the target gets instead; see below.

Which rate applies: for each source compartment, the entry that matches with the most conditions wins; on a tie, the first one in the list. With no match, the fallback rate applies. With three stratifications and one entry for g2, t1, v2:

Source compartment Conditions matched Rate A_g2_t1_v2 3 of 3 The entry A_g2_t1_v1 not all Fallback A_g1_t1_v1 not all Fallback

docs.title: Redirecting the target with to
docs.text:
A condition with category filters the source. A condition with to changes the target category. A condition with only to filters nothing, so it can send the flow into a stratification that the source does not have:

redirect = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Redirect")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_stratification(id="group", categories=["g1", "g2"])
    .add_stratification(
        id="subtype",
        categories=["s1", "s2"],
        conditions=[{"stratification": "group", "category": "g2"}],
    )
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(
        id="move",
        source=["g1"],
        target=["g2"],
        stratified_rates=[{"conditions": [{"stratification": "subtype", "to": "s1"}], "rate": "k"}],
    )
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.5, "B": 0.5},
            stratification_fractions={
                "group": {"g1": 0.5, "g2": 0.5},
                "subtype": {"s1": 0.5, "s2": 0.5},
            },
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)
print(redirect.describe().render("text"))
# A_g1 -> A_g2_s1: k * A_g1   and   B_g1 -> B_g2_s1: k * B_g1

docs.title: Limiting when a transition runs
docs.text: A transition runs at every step. To limit a flow, write the condition in the rate with if, as in "if(step > 30, k, 0)", or use a AxisPattern, a series parameter or a stratified rate. A comparison alone is a boolean, so "k * (step > 30)" is rejected.

docs.title: Impulses
docs.text:
An impulse moves its amount at once, at given steps, and nothing between them. Give the steps with impulse_at=[…] or impulse_every=(period, offset). The rate is then a fraction of the source (proportional) or an amount (absolute), with the same rules, sources, targets, stratified rates and accumulators as any transition.

impulse_model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Impulses")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_accumulator(id="moved", name="Moved by the impulse")
    .add_parameter(id="p", value=0.25)
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=0.1)
    .add_transition(id="jump", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="p", impulse_at=[1], accumulators=["moved"])
    .add_transition(id="flow", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

jumped = Simulation(impulse_model).run(num_steps=2)
print([round(a, 1) for a in jumped["A"]])  # [1000.0, 675.0, 607.5]
print(jumped["moved"][2])  # 225.0: a quarter of the 900 left at step 1
Rule In both engines Order At step n the state jumps first; then the flows of the step run from the new state. The output at n shows the state after the jump (CompiledModel::apply_impulses in crates/commol-model/src/system.rs). Several impulses at one step Every jump is computed from the state before any of them. Steps A DifferentialEquations model takes any steps, such as 0.5: the engine stops there, applies the jump and restarts. A DifferenceEquations model needs integer steps (ValidationError names the transition). Units The rate of an impulse is an amount, <bin unit>, not a flow per step (Units). describe() Lists impulses apart from the equations, with their steps (Describing a Model).

An impulse is not a pulse rate. A AxisPattern.pulse is a rate: a difference model applies it for one step with the other flows, and a differential model applies it as a constant rate for one unit of the axis, so it moves 1 − e^(−p) of its source. An impulse moves exactly p of its source in both engines.

docs.title: Amounts below zero
docs.text:
A DifferenceEquations step never leaves a compartment below zero. After the impulses of a step and after its flows, the engine checks every compartment. An amount below −10⁻¹² × total (the total at the start of the step) stops the run with InfeasibleStateError, a ValueError. The message names the compartment, the step, its amount before the step and the flows out of it, largest first. The tolerance lets a flow that empties a compartment exactly pass. Accumulators are not checked: a net flow may count negative (DifferenceEquations::step in crates/commol-difference/src/simulation.rs).

from commol import InfeasibleStateError

too_fast = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Too fast")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k", value=1.5)
    .add_transition(id="t", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

try:
    Simulation(too_fast).run(num_steps=3)
except InfeasibleStateError as error:
    print(error)  # The flows of step 0 leave compartment 'A' at -500, ...

A step moves what the flows give, so the usual causes are in the rates:

Cause Example Fix Proportional rates that sum above 1 rate="k" with k = 1.5 moves 1.5 times its source in one step A smaller rate per step, or a shorter step An absolute rate on a bin total With stratifications, "k1 * A * B / total" moves from each compartment of A an amount computed from the total of A per_compartment=True, so each compartment loses an amount from its own amount (per_compartment) A rate that turns negative "k * B * (1 - C / capacity)" once C > capacity: the flow runs backwards and drains its target Bound the factor: "k * B * max(0, 1 - C / capacity)"

A calibration gives a run that stops this way a penalty and goes on; see Calibration. A DifferentialEquations model is not checked: its solver may step below zero by its tolerance.

docs.title: What building checks
docs.text:
build plans every flow in the engine and rejects a transition it cannot simulate as written:

Rejected Message names A source or target that is neither a bin nor a category of one stratification The transition A category transition without exactly one source and one target The transition A rate variable that is not a parameter, bin, compartment or special variable The variable and the available names Several sources with a proportional rate The transition; use an absolute rate or $compartment A stratified rate whose category conditions match no source compartment The categories; use to to reach another stratification A flow that ends in categories no compartment has The transition; add a to condition impulse_at and impulse_every together, a negative step, or a period that is not positive The transition A non-integer impulse step in a DifferenceEquations model The transition and the step

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Back to Building Models

Commol checks that every rate of a built Model has the right units. To see the equations the engine simulates, with their units, see Describing a Model.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import Aggregate, ModelBuilder

model = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Model with Units", bin_unit="item", step_unit="day")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="1/day")
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1, "C": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

model.check_unit_consistency(verbose=True)  # Unit consistency check passed successfully.

docs.title: Unit checking
docs.text: Model.check_unit_consistency(verbose=False) checks that every flow has the unit <bin unit>/<step unit>, every impulse the unit <bin unit>, and that every function receives a plain number. It checks DifferenceEquations and DifferentialEquations models alike: in both, a rate is per unit of the axis, and only what its value means differs (see What a rate means). It reads the flows the engine plans (transition_flows), so a proportional rate is checked as its flow, the rate times its source: k2 in 1/day from a bin in item gives item/day. A rate that reads the neighbors of a unit is checked as the sums they are. It raises UnitConsistencyError (from commol.utils.equations) and lists every transition that fails.

docs.title: What needs a unit
docs.text:
Item How it gets a unit Bins ModelBuilder(bin_unit=...), or add_bin(unit=...) for one bin. Required: the check names every bin without one. total, total_<category>… The bin unit, automatically Constant parameters add_parameter(unit=...). Required: the check raises if one is missing. Formula parameters Inferred from the formula; a unit is optional t The step unit, automatically: it is a position on the axis step, pi, e Dimensionless, automatically: step counts increments Unit Use for "1/day", "1/week", "1/step" Rates "dimensionless" Ratios, fractions, amplitudes, function arguments Any word that pint does not define, such as "item" A unit of its own dimension; Commol registers it

A unit means what pint defines, for time as for any other quantity: month, year and fortnight are units of time, but quarter is a unit of mass and decade is a number. A word that pint does not define, such as mo, becomes a unit of its own dimension, which no other unit converts to.

docs.title: The step unit
docs.text:
The engine converts no value between units. So one step has one unit, and every rate must use it (UnitChecker._step_unit in py-commol/commol/context/_model/units.py).

The axis of a model is its independent variable: the quantity the model steps along or differentiates over. Time is one case; a length, a dose or any other quantity is another. So the step unit may have any single dimension. Declare it with ModelBuilder(..., step_unit="day") (Model.step_unit); check_step_unit accepts one unit of one dimension with exponent 1, such as day or meter, and rejects 1/day or meter**2. A model that declares no step unit has the step unit step, the default increment of any axis, of its own dimension [step]. The check never guesses the step unit from the parameters.

Model Step unit Flows must be step_unit="day" day <bin unit>/day: a rate in 1/d passes, a rate in 1/week or 1/quarter fails step_unit="meter" meter <bin unit>/meter No step_unit, rates in 1/step or none step <bin unit>/step No step_unit, rates in 1/day step Fails; the error says to declare step_unit

Two names of one unit, such as d and day, are one unit. A flow must have exactly the expected unit: item/week does not match item/day, because the engine would read a weekly rate as a daily one.

along_a_line = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Along a line", bin_unit="item", step_unit="meter")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.01, unit="1/meter")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 1.0, "B": 0.0},
        ),
        engine="DifferentialEquations",
    )
)
along_a_line.check_unit_consistency(verbose=True)  # Unit consistency check passed successfully.

Model.axis_units() converts values in units of the step dimension to steps, and gives the rates the engine reads; see Units of the axis.

docs.title: Positions and numbers in a rate
docs.text:
t is a position on the axis, so it has the step unit: with step_unit="day", k * t * A passes when k is in 1/day**2. step counts increments and is dimensionless.

A number written in a rate and added to, subtracted from or compared with a quantity is read in the unit of that quantity, as the engine reads it: if(t >= 10, k, 0) compares t with 10 days, and t - 3 is 3 days before t. The two branches of if and the arguments of min and max must share a unit, and a written 0 takes the unit of the other branch. A number that a function computes, such as exp(2), stays dimensionless.

docs.title: Impulses
docs.text: An impulse moves an amount at once, so its rate must have the bin unit: p * A with p in "dimensionless" is an amount of <bin unit>; k * A with k in "1/day" is a flow and fails with expected '<bin unit>'.

docs.title: What the check catches
docs.text:
from commol.utils.equations import UnitConsistencyError

wrong_units = (
    ModelBuilder(name="Wrong units", bin_unit="item", step_unit="day")
    .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
    .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
    .add_parameter(id="k1", value=0.5, unit="day")  # should be "1/day"
    .add_parameter(id="k2", value=0.1, unit="1/day")
    .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
    .add_transition(id="t_ba", source=["B"], target=["A"], rate="k2 * sin(B) * B")
    .build(
        Aggregate(
            total=1000,
            bin_fractions={"A": 0.9, "B": 0.1},
        ),
        engine="DifferenceEquations",
    )
)

try:
    wrong_units.check_unit_consistency()
except UnitConsistencyError as error:
    print(error)
Error Cause Unit mismatch: equation '…' has unit 'day * item' but expected 'item/day' A rate with the wrong unit Cannot convert from 'item' to 'dimensionless' A function such as sin, exp or log received a quantity with a unit The following constant parameters are missing units: … A constant parameter has no unit The following bins have no unit: … A bin has no unit (set bin_unit) The model declares no step unit, so it is 'step' Rates in a unit such as 1/day without step_unit; see The step unit Variable '…' … has no defined unit A variable of a rate has no unit

To pass a quantity to a function, make it dimensionless first, for example sin(2 * pi * step / 365) or exp(-decay * step) with decay in "dimensionless", or sin(2 * pi * t / period) with period in the step unit.

docs.title: Uncertainty
docs.text:
Back to Home

A calibration gives one set of parameters. This section shows how far you can trust it: which parameters the data identify, how the inputs move the outputs, and whether the intervals you report cover what they claim. This page defines what every method returns and reads: a weighted parameter sample, the predictive of a sample, and the scores that check it against data. Each method has its own page, listed in the table below.

docs.title: The three questions
docs.text: Question What answers it Which parameters fit the data? The identifiability methods; a sample of the parameters, or a profile of the loss; several starts that end apart with equal losses show that the data do not identify the parameters How do the inputs move the outputs? The predictive of a sample: the run of every draw, and its band Are the intervals calibrated? Scores of the predictive against observations the method did not see, and coverage studies

docs.title: A band of the model, or a prediction interval
docs.text: A band of the model is the spread of the model's output across the draws of the parameters. It says where the model curve lies, not where the next observation will fall: an observation also carries measurement noise. A prediction interval adds that noise to every draw before it reduces them (the ObservationNoise port of commol-inference). A method that has no noise model gives a band of the model, and this page says so wherever it shows one. Comparing a band of the model with data underestimates the spread, so its coverage of the data is below its level.

docs.title: Which method answers which question
docs.text:
Method Question Needs a noise model Page Several starts, Calibrator.run(starts=n) Which parameters fit the data: distinct ends with equal losses No Optimizers StructuralRank Which parameters any data of this design can determine, and which combinations No Identifiability Collinearity Which parameters can be fitted together No Identifiability SampleIdentifiability Which parameters a sample determines: contraction, correlations, modes No Identifiability StartsIdentifiability Which parameters differ between starts of equal loss No Identifiability

Each uncertainty method adds its row here when it lands.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
from commol import (
    Aggregate,
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    ModelBuilder,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    ObservedDataPoint,
    ParameterSample,
    Predictive,
    SampleMethod,
    Simulation,
    scores,
)


def basic_model(k1: float | None, k2: float | None):
    return (
        ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
        .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
        .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
        .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
        .add_parameter(id="k1", value=k1)
        .add_parameter(id="k2", value=k2)
        .add_transition(id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * A * B / total")
        .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
        .build(
            Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0}),
            engine="DifferenceEquations",
        )
    )


truth = Simulation(basic_model(0.4, 0.1)).run(num_steps=60)
observations = [
    ObservedDataPoint(at=step, output="B", value=truth["B"][step])
    for step in range(5, 61, 5)
]
# Fit the first 40 steps; hold out the rest to check the predictive.
fitted = [point for point in observations if point.at <= 40]
held_out = [point for point in observations if point.at > 40]

problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=fitted,
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k1", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.0, max_bound=1.0),
        CalibrationParameter(id="k2", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.0, max_bound=1.0),
    ],
    loss_function="sse",
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=2000),
    seed=42,
)
calibrator = Calibrator(Simulation(basic_model(None, None)), problem)

# A sample of the parameters. A method returns one; here it is written by hand.
sample = ParameterSample.equally_weighted(
    names=["k1", "k2"],
    bounds=[(0.0, 1.0), (0.0, 1.0)],
    values=[[0.38, 0.09], [0.40, 0.10], [0.42, 0.11]],
    method=SampleMethod(name="by hand"),
)
print(sample.interval(0.9)["k1"])  # (0.38, 0.42)

# The predictive: every draw run to step 60, and its band of the model.
predictive = Predictive(calibrator, sample, positions=list(range(61)))
band = predictive.band(confidence_level=0.9)
print(band.lower["B"][50] <= truth["B"][50] <= band.upper["B"][50])  # True

# Scores on the held-out observations.
print(scores.coverage(predictive, held_out, confidence_level=0.9).mean)
print(scores.crps(predictive, held_out).per_series)

docs.title: The parameter sample
docs.text:
A ParameterSample holds draws of the parameters of one problem, each with a weight. Every method with draws returns one; the plots, the reports, the predictive and the scores read it, never the result of a method.

Field Meaning names One name per column, in the order of the problem's parameters bounds The bounds of each parameter; every value lies inside them values One row per draw log_weights The log weight of each draw, normalized so the weights sum to 1; -inf for a weight of zero groups The chain, replicate or wave of each draw, or None method The name and settings of the method that made it (SampleMethod)

Every statistic is weighted and computed in Rust. With equal weights it is the unweighted statistic.

Member Returns mean() The weighted mean of each parameter covariance(), correlation() Weighted matrices, in the order of names; with equal weights, NumPy's cov and corrcoef quantiles(levels), interval(confidence_level) Weighted quantiles by the one convention effective_size() Kish's effective sample size, 1 / Σ wᵢ² draws() One {name: value} mapping per draw resample(count, seed) A sample of equal weights, drawn by weight summary(confidence_level) A ParameterSummary per parameter, for a report 
print(round(sample.effective_size(), 6))  # 3.0
print(next(sample.draws()))  # {'k1': 0.38, 'k2': 0.09}

A sample has no single set of parameters, so Model.apply_calibration_parameters rejects it with a TypeError; apply one of sample.draws(). A sample saves to JSON and loads back equal (model_dump_json, model_validate_json).

docs.title: The one quantile
docs.text:
Every interval of commol is a weighted quantile: the inverse of the weighted empirical distribution, interpolated between the midpoints of the cumulative weights. With equal weights it equals numpy.percentile(..., method="hazen"). A draw of weight zero does not count. weighted_quantiles computes it for any values, and member_statistics reduces ensemble members with it.

from commol import weighted_quantiles

print(weighted_quantiles([0.0, 1.0], levels=[0.5], weights=[1.0, 3.0]))  # [0.75]

docs.title: The predictive
docs.text:
Predictive(calibrator, sample, positions) runs every draw at positions, in parallel in Rust. With a stochastic engine every replicate of a draw is a draw of the predictive, with an equal share of its weight.

Member Returns band(confidence_level) The weighted mean, median and central interval of every output at every position (PredictiveBand) series_band(outputs, confidence_level, cumulative=False) The band of the sum of some outputs, or of its running total; each draw is reduced first at_observations(observed_data) Every draw's value of each observation, read through the observation operator the loss uses: sums, windows and factors (ObservationDraws) runs(), weights The trajectory and weight of every draw

SimulationPlotter.plot_series and plot_cumulative draw the band of a predictive when it is the calibration_result, and simulation_report reduces its draws with their weights when it is the ensemble_runs. applied_parameters_report takes the sample itself (sample=, with a confidence_level).

docs.title: Scores
docs.text:
The functions of commol.scores compare a predictive with observations, and return a Score: the value of each observation, the mean of each series and the overall mean. Which observations to score is an argument with no default: score data the method did not see, such as the held-out positions above.

Function Score Better coverage(predictive, observations, confidence_level) 1 inside the central interval, 0 outside; the mean is the empirical coverage Close to the level interval_score(predictive, observations, confidence_level) (u − l) + (2/α)(l − y)₊ + (2/α)(y − u)₊, α = 1 − c Lower weighted_interval_score(predictive, observations, confidence_levels) The weighted interval score of Bracher et al. (2021) Lower crps(predictive, observations) Σ wᵢ|xᵢ − y| − ½ Σᵢⱼ wᵢwⱼ|xᵢ − xⱼ|, the CRPS of a stochastic calibration's loss Lower pit(predictive, observations, seed) F(y), randomized where draws tie with y Uniform

docs.title: The entry point
docs.text:
Every method runs through Calibrator.uncertainty(method). A method is a configuration, a subclass of UncertaintyMethod[R] whose type parameter R is its result; the call returns an R, which a static type checker infers from the configuration's type. A configuration with no registered runner raises a ValueError that names the registered ones.

The identifiability methods run through their own entry point, Calibrator.identifiability(method), with a subclass of IdentifiabilityMethod[R]: they answer another question (Identifiability). Both kinds subclass InferenceMethod[R] and share one registry; each entry point refuses the other kind with a TypeError that names the right one.

result = calibrator.uncertainty(SomeMethod(...))

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] You report a band of the model as a band of the model, not as a prediction interval.
  • [ ] You score observations the method did not see.
  • [ ] The effective size of a weighted sample is large enough for the intervals you read.

docs.title: Identifiability
docs.text:
Back to Uncertainty

A parameter the data cannot determine shows up as a wide interval, or as starts that end apart with equal losses. This page shows how to find out why: which parameters the model and the data determine, which they do not, and which combination of parameters the data determine in their place. It is for anyone who fits more than one parameter.

docs.title: Structural against practical
docs.text:
Kind Question Depends on Methods Structural Can any data from this design determine the parameter? The model and the positions and outputs observed, not the observed values StructuralRank Practical Do these data determine it? The observed values, their noise and the fit Collinearity, SampleIdentifiability, StartsIdentifiability

A parameter that is not structurally identifiable is never practically identifiable: no amount of data of the same design fixes it. A parameter that is structurally identifiable can still be poorly determined by the data at hand.

docs.title: Quick path
docs.text:
k1 and alpha enter the model only as their product k1 * alpha, so the data determine the product and not each one.

from commol import (
    Aggregate,
    CalibrationParameter,
    CalibrationProblem,
    Calibrator,
    Collinearity,
    ModelBuilder,
    NelderMeadConfig,
    ObservedDataPoint,
    ParameterSample,
    SampleIdentifiability,
    SampleMethod,
    Simulation,
    StartsIdentifiability,
    StructuralRank,
    identifiability_report,
)


def basic_model(k1: float | None, alpha: float | None, k2: float | None):
    return (
        ModelBuilder(name="Basic Model")
        .add_bin(id="A", name="State A")
        .add_bin(id="B", name="State B")
        .add_bin(id="C", name="State C")
        .add_parameter(id="k1", value=k1)
        .add_parameter(id="alpha", value=alpha)
        .add_parameter(id="k2", value=k2)
        .add_transition(
            id="t_ab", source=["A"], target=["B"], rate="k1 * alpha * A * B / total"
        )
        .add_transition(id="t_bc", source=["B"], target=["C"], rate="k2 * B")
        .build(
            Aggregate(total=1000, bin_fractions={"A": 0.99, "B": 0.01, "C": 0.0}),
            engine="DifferenceEquations",
        )
    )


truth = Simulation(basic_model(0.4, 1.0, 0.1)).run(num_steps=60)
problem = CalibrationProblem(
    observed_data=[
        # B with a measurement error of ±5 %.
        ObservedDataPoint(at=step, output="B", value=truth["B"][step] * (1 + 0.05 * (-1) ** step))
        for step in range(5, 61, 5)
    ],
    parameters=[
        CalibrationParameter(id="k1", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.1, max_bound=1.0),
        CalibrationParameter(id="alpha", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.5, max_bound=2.0),
        CalibrationParameter(id="k2", parameter_type="parameter", min_bound=0.01, max_bound=0.5),
    ],
    loss_function="sse",
    optimization_config=NelderMeadConfig(max_iterations=2000),
    seed=42,
)
calibrator = Calibrator(Simulation(basic_model(None, None, None)), problem)

# Before a fit: the structure of the model and the design.
structural = calibrator.identifiability(StructuralRank(points=5, design="observations"))
for name, verdicts in structural.verdicts.items():
    print(name, verdicts.structural.verdict, verdicts.structural.combinations)
# k1 in_combination ['k1 · alpha']
# alpha in_combination ['k1 · alpha']
# k2 identifiable []

# After a fit: the starts and the collinearity at the best point.
result = calibrator.run(starts=6)
starts = calibrator.identifiability(
    StartsIdentifiability(result=result, parameter_tolerance=0.05, loss_tolerance=0.01)
)
print(starts.starts[0].flagged)  # ['k1', 'alpha']
collinearity = calibrator.identifiability(
    Collinearity(at=result, max_subset_size=3, threshold=10)
)
print([subset.parameters for subset in collinearity.collinearity[0].admissible])
# [['k1', 'k2'], ['alpha', 'k2']]

# One report with every piece of evidence.
report = structural.merge(starts, collinearity)
for name, verdicts in report.verdicts.items():
    print(name, verdicts.structural.verdict, verdicts.practical.verdict)
# k1 in_combination poorly_determined
# alpha in_combination poorly_determined
# k2 identifiable determined

Fix alpha (or k1) at a value, or calibrate their product as one parameter: the data determine k1 · alpha, and the fit says nothing about how it splits.

docs.title: The methods
docs.text:
Every method runs through Calibrator.identifiability(method) and returns an IdentifiabilityReport. A threshold or a tolerance has no default: it is a modelling judgment, and the table gives the range the literature uses.

Method Needs Answers Engine StructuralRank(points, design, seed=None) The problem only The rank of the sensitivities, the non-identifiable parameters and the identifiable combinations Deterministic Collinearity(at, max_subset_size, threshold) A fit (CalibrationResult) or a sample Which subsets of parameters can be fitted together; threshold from 5 to 20 Deterministic SampleIdentifiability(sample, reference, correlation_threshold) Any ParameterSample How much the sample contracts each parameter, which pairs move together, which marginals have several modes; correlation_threshold from 0.8 to 0.95 Any StartsIdentifiability(result, parameter_tolerance, loss_tolerance) A result of Calibrator.run(starts=n) with two or more converged starts Which parameters differ between starts of equal loss Any

docs.title: Structural rank
docs.text:
StructuralRank evaluates the sensitivities of the predicted observations at points rows of a Latin hypercube over the bounds, drawn from seed (the problem's seed by default). The sensitivity of observation i to parameter j is scaled to a relative change of both, S_ij = (∂y_i/∂θ_j) · θ_j / s_i, where s_i is the root mean square of the series of observation i, so the answer does not depend on units.

design Positions and outputs Question "observations" Those of the problem's observations; their values are ignored Can this design determine the parameters? "dense" Every observed series, with its outputs, factor and window, at every unit position from 0 to the last observation Can denser data of the same series determine them?

At each point the rank counts the singular values of S above the norm of the estimated error of S. The generic rank is the rank at most points; each point's singular values are in report.structural[0].points. A parameter is:

Verdict Meaning identifiable No combination of the other parameters undoes a change of it in_combination Only the combinations in combinations are identifiable non_identifiable No observation changes with it

Only the design of the observations gives the structural verdict of a parameter; a dense design keeps its verdicts in its section.

dense = calibrator.identifiability(StructuralRank(points=5, design="dense"))
print(dense.structural[0].generic_rank, dense.structural[0].verdicts["k1"])
# 2 in_combination

Denser data of B do not split the product either: the deficit is in the model, not in the design.

docs.title: How to read a combination
docs.text: A combination is a product of powers of the parameters that the data determine: k1 · alpha means that every pair (k1, alpha) with the same product fits the data equally well. k1 / k2^2 means that k1 and k2² can grow together. A parameter whose bounds allow negative values reads as its absolute value, |k1|. The exponents are rounded to the nearest half.

docs.title: Collinearity
docs.text:
Collinearity computes, after Brun et al. (2001), the sensitivity measure of each parameter and the collinearity index γ of each subset: 1 when the sensitivities of the subset are orthogonal, infinite when one is a combination of the others. A subset with γ below threshold can be fitted together; admissible lists the largest such subsets. With a sample, the index is computed at every draw and summarized by its weighted median, and share_below gives the share of the draws below the threshold.

A parameter is poorly_determined when a pair that holds it has an index at or above the threshold, or no observation is sensitive to it.

docs.title: A sample
docs.text:
SampleIdentifiability reads any sample, such as the draws of an uncertainty method. Here the sample is the ends of the starts.

names = calibrator.parameter_names
sample = ParameterSample.equally_weighted(
    names,
    [(p.min_bound, p.max_bound) for p in problem.parameters],
    [[start.end[name] for name in names] for start in result.starts],
    SampleMethod(name="starts"),
)
from_sample = calibrator.identifiability(
    SampleIdentifiability(sample=sample, reference="bounds", correlation_threshold=0.9)
)
pair = from_sample.sample[0].correlated_pairs[0]
print(pair.first, pair.second, round(pair.correlation, 1))  # k1 alpha -1.0
Field Meaning contraction 1 − Var(sample) / Var(reference): near 0 when the sample spreads over the bounds, near 1 when it sits on one value correlated_pairs The pairs whose absolute correlation is above correlation_threshold modes The modes of each marginal: the maxima of a kernel density above a tenth of the highest

A parameter is poorly_determined when it is in a correlated pair or its marginal has two or more modes.

docs.title: Starts
docs.text: StartsIdentifiability compares the converged starts whose loss exceeds the best by at most loss_tolerance of the best loss, and flags a parameter whose ends among them differ by more than parameter_tolerance of its bound width. A loss near zero, as with data made by the model itself, leaves no start within a relative tolerance but the best; use data with noise.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
An IdentifiabilityReport holds, for each parameter, a structural and a practical verdict, and the sections of the methods that ran (structural, collinearity, sample, starts). merge joins reports: a verdict the reports agree on stays, with every reason; one they disagree on is conflicting, with both reasons. identifiability_report gives it as plain data.

data = identifiability_report(report)
print(data["parameters"]["k2"]["practical"]["verdict"])  # determined

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Local. The sensitivities are derivatives at points: a parameter can be identifiable near every point and still have two distant values that fit equally well. Symbolic methods give a global answer for differential equations; they are outside commol.
  • Numerical. The derivatives are finite differences; a singular value counts only when it is above their estimated error. The error grows with the tolerance of an ODE solver (rtol).
  • Generic points. A point where the rank is lower or higher than at most points is special; the generic rank is the rank at most points.
  • Deterministic engines. The runs of a stochastic engine change in jumps with the parameters, so StructuralRank and Collinearity refuse one; SampleIdentifiability and StartsIdentifiability accept it.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] You checked the structural rank of the design before you fitted.
  • [ ] Each parameter in_combination is fixed, or replaced by its combination.
  • [ ] The thresholds you chose are in the report you share.
